name: He Who Fights With Monsters | Compendium Lorebook (spoiler level 2)
description: Derived from the HWFWM compendium (not a source). Spoiler level 2: Books 1-9. Book text takes precedence over the fan wiki; this file is regenerated by src/tools/lorebook.py.

key: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*
1.comment: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*
1.content: This primer is the foundation of the compendium. It explains the setting in plain language and summarises the facts that come up again and again. Later documents expand every section. Where a fact only becomes true later in the story it is marked (Later: Book N). The series follows Jason Asano, an ordinary Australian who is pulled out of his world by an accident and arrives, hairless and alone, in Pallimustus: a world very like Earth in size and shape, but soaked in magic. There, people absorb essences (crystallised magic), which give them supernatural abilities, and grow through ranks by hunting monsters and training. Adventurers, guilds, gods and rulers all depend on this system. Pallimustus has a twin, Earth, which was made from the same template but has much less magic, so its people do not know magic exists (at first). The two worlds are linked, and the link matters more and more as the story proceeds. Above both worlds sits a larger cosmos of great astral beings, gods, astral kings and other powers who rarely interact directly with mortals but shape their lives. In a roleplay you can set a story anywhere from the beginning (a rural iron-rank adventurer in Greenstone) to the end (a gold-rank world-defender at the edge of a cosmic war). Jason's powers revolve around afflictions (long-lasting debilitating effects). Many characters' signature lines are used as incantations ("Feed me your sins", "Mine is the judgement, and the judgement is death").
keys: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*
1.name: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*

2.content: Astral kings rule their own universes. Most are messengers' masters: the messengers are their servants, invaders of worlds, and carry the astral king's message. In Book 8 Jason discovers that he himself is an astral king, which makes him both a political danger among the messengers and an unusual ally to them.
2.name: Astral Kings and Messengers

3.content: Authority is what great astral beings and gods are made of, and the thing that lets them shape the cosmos. It cannot be taken by force and must be traded, it comes in a safe set state and a dangerous potential state, and it is guided by will. Sanctioning is how transcendent beings change one another: their authority is turned against them, or they change themselves with it. The books treat it as the cosmos's only real punishment, because an immortal cannot be killed. What it is: great astral beings are the most powerful entities in the cosmos, and "the nature of both themselves and their power was known as authority". Authority is "the fundamental power of the cosmos", and everything in physical reality is underpinned by it to some degree. Two states: set-state authority has been put to a purpose, which makes it fixed, defined and safe ("clay turned into a bowl"); potential-state authority is the unworked clay, "except the clay is actually enriched uranium". Jason's domains: his spirit domains are made of set-state authority, which he calls "the treehouse that I'm allowed to play in". His spirit realm is also an aspect of his authority. He thinks that if his domains broke down into potential-state authority it would kill him. Transformation zones: they are "areas of set-state authority breaking down into potential-state authority", the domes being the world sealing them like scabs.
3.name: Authority and Sanctioning

4.content: Gods are transcendent beings outside physical reality, each focused on a single concept (Dominion, Healer, Knowledge, Death and more). They manifest avatars, speak with Akashic Speech, give followers essences and awakening stones that they can take back, and work miracles. In Jason's words in Book 8, "gods are like regional managers of full-blown universes". Churches are their institutions.
4.name: Gods and Churches

5.content: A great astral being (GAB) is a cosmic-scale transcendent: an aspect of the cosmos that embodies a concept such as construction, finality of death, time, entropy or dimensional integrity. They are not gods and are not bound by gods. Clive describes them in Book 1 as similar to gods but belonging to no world: they exist between worlds in the deep astral, "gods to the gods, although you wouldn't catch any gods saying that". They do not rule worlds directly. They act through vessels: mortals chosen to host them, and prime vessels, who carry the fullest part of their power. GABs cannot interact with physical reality directly; they recruit others to act for them. Authority: they generate it intrinsically. See 00_Cosmology_Overview.md. Mortal form: great astral beings enjoy mortal bodies. A vessel can be possessed; Clive notes it is possible, if far from ethical. Diamond-rank vessels of the great astral beings can withstand the strain and keep their selves, unlike the disposable vessels the Builder uses; eventually the soul can no longer cope and the vessel passes on the role, with no lingering effects and a stronger soul as a result. No fear of gods: Clive says a GAB is one of the few beings that need not fear a god's retribution, since the gods of Pallimustus cannot see into an astral space that is not part of their world. Sanctioning: see section 4. Dawn tells Shako in Book 6 that by killing Jason he violated the compact between the Builder, the Reaper and the World-Phoenix.
5.name: Great Astral Beings

6.content: The astral is the space between worlds, the source of all magic, and the home of the beings who govern the cosmos. Clive explains it to Jason as a bowl of dumpling soup in which worlds float. The deep astral has no geography, time or space of its own, and gold-rankers rarely travel in it without a patron. Interstice, the universe-city, is the capital of the part of it that anyone knows. The dumpling soup: Clive says the cosmos is "a bowl of dumpling soup". Each physical reality is a dumpling, and "the astral is the soup through which we are all the dumplings... floating". The astral is also the source of all magic, "pure, unadulterated; the most fundamental building blocks of reality". Why worlds differ: some worlds soak up a lot of the soup and others very little, which is why Pallimustus has essences, awakening stones, quintessence and monsters and Earth did not. Astral spaces: "think of the soup kind of congealing around a dumpling", giving a magical dimension attached to a world. Congealed magic can drift away, especially if someone pokes a hole in the world's side, and can touch another world to form a brief unstable link. What the deep astral is: "just magic. Only magic." Physical substance cannot exist there, which is why Jason's body "ceased to exist" when he was pulled through it. Only his soul, being magical, survived.
6.name: The Deep Astral and Interstice

7.content: The god of Death on Pallimustus governs the passage of souls into the astral, and is distinct from the Reaper, the great astral being who is "very big on the finality of death". The church certifies deaths and returns, opposes Undeath, and is dryly protective of the order of things. The deity changes guise, and the books speak of both a goddess and a lord. Domain: the Reaper is "very big on the finality of death. Some consider it the true god of death, as all our god of death governs is the passage of the soul into the astral". Where there is no god of death to guide the soul into the astral, it drifts into the Reaper's grasp on its own.
7.name: Death

8.content: Dominion is the god of rulership, the god "of deciding who gets to be king". He is young, handsome, sneering, charming and frank, he is the god most interested in Jason, and he turns up in person more often than any other. His church is the outlier among churches in keeping low-ranking essence users under its thumb. For all his menace he gives Jason surprisingly honest advice. The temple and the creed: a believer in the Divine Square calls it the temple of Dominion and says "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles. It is he who determines who rules, and who serves". First appearance: at Jory's clinic he comes to take the Healer's cast-out clergy, "young and handsome, but with a look of disdain and faint cruelty", with an aura like a wave of fire. He tells those who join: "There is no service in my church... under me, you will obey or suffer. Or both, as I choose, because you will not enter my service. You will belong to me". Jason and Gary: "I love that guy," Dominion says of Jason, because "the ones who won't kneel are always the most fun". He tests Gary with his gaze, laughs when Gary stands, and says "That is where monarchs come from. I love them most of all. I'll be keeping an eye on you, Gareth Xandier". He asked after Jason by name.
8.name: Dominion

9.content: Fertility is the god of growth and birth, and his church is far more practical than its murals suggest. Its temples are covered in murals of people being fertile, which Jason notes with some alarm. The murals: Jason avoids pairing with "the god of fertility? The one with all the provocative murals?", and Farrah describes the temples as covered "in murals of people... being fertile".
9.name: Fertility

10.content: The goddess of Knowledge is the god Jason meets first and speaks to most. She is detached, polite, honest in form and a planner at heart, and she knows everything anyone in her world knows. Her church is scholarly and wealthy and funds research, and from Book 6 on it is shown mustering armies. Appearance: in the Divine Square a glorious light appears in front of a temple and the people fall to their knees. In her temple she takes the form of a woman with colourful clothes and Mediterranean features, "beautiful, yet there was something detached and untouchable about her". She says "I am Knowledge. Everything that is, or ever was known in this world". Omniscience, limited: she knows what anyone in her world knows, including what Jason brought with him. Jason says in a recording that deities are gender fluid, "heard from the goddess of knowledge herself", and jokes that she knows his Mario Kart shortcuts. The church: acolytes of the church check Adventure Society assessments, "don't try to slip anything past them, because there isn't any point". Gabrielle Pellin introduces herself as an acolyte. Danielle Geller will send her scholarly relatives to the temple's library, as "the goddess always welcomes seekers of truth". Gifts to Jason: a token the goddess claimed would send him home and books on dimensional transgression, which Clive annotates.
10.name: Knowledge

11.content: Pain and Discord belong to the "hidden" gods, the gods people pray to for what they want to avoid. The books mention them only in passing. This file records every thing the text says, so that a story using them knows how much is open. The hidden gods: Carlos says many gods fall into two camps: those whose temples are anywhere there are people, and "the gods whose priests dwell in the hidden places. Gods who you pray to not because of something you want, but something you want to avoid. Pain, Discord, Deceit". These are the "dark gods" who "will do very well" if the Purity deception becomes public, and Carlos does not like "the idea of my actions serving the God of Discord". Pain, a god or a goddess: a soldier thinks of Pain as a god, but Kerr answers, "Where I come from, they know that Pain is a woman", and refers to "the Goddess of Pain's firstborn daughter". Gods are gender-fluid in the books. A byword for fear: Trenchant says that against an affliction skirmisher he would "run like the God of Pain was chasing me". Discord: it is called out as "in particular" the god the deception benefits.
11.name: Pain and Discord

12.content: Purity is the god of cleanliness, with both gentle and extreme aspects; his church is rich, strict and prominent in Greenstone. The church: Anisa Lasalle is a priestess of the God of Purity, and a priest of Purity in clean robes attends the Adventure Society inquiry team. The temple has church militants who guard its interests. Collusion with the Builder cult: when the church's involvement with the cult comes to light, a number of its key members vanish on "previously scheduled sabbaticals", including the archbishop Nicolas Hedron. The people from the church are detained under the authority of the ecumenical council. Hendren: the archbishop calls out, "You think afflictions can take down a priest of Purity?" in the fight.
12.name: Purity and Disguise

13.content: The god of medicine and healing, the Healer is kind, modest in manner and strict with those who exploit the sick. His church runs clinics, hospitals and research. In Book 1 he casts out the corrupt clergy of the Greenstone temple in person, and in later books his priests, among them Neil, Carlos and Arabelle, are central members of Jason's team. Corruption in Greenstone: Neil Davone makes a stand in the Greenstone Temple of the Healer, saying "This isn't about serving the Healer", and is told he is no longer welcome in the church. The god arrives: the Healer appears at Jory's clinic, tells his clergy that merely not being shunned from his temples is "mercy enough", and refuses to restore their essences: "For that, I shall give you no salve. But you may turn to another". He says the power-seekers are of no use to him and hands them to Dominion, who takes those willing. A blessing: he declares the clinic a sanctuary for healing, accepts that Jory's alchemy includes "togetherness jelly" ("I'm not going to begrudge people a little... togetherness"), and promises rituals of sanctification and a healer to staff it. Those who repent: he answers a plea from a priest with "You blame others for your failings?", and gives a slight nod of assent to those who accept responsibility.
13.name: The Healer

14.content: The All-Devouring Eye is the great astral being of annihilation. It does not communicate with the others, gives no blessings, and stands apart from the pacts. Among those interested: it is one of the handful of great astral beings that take an interest in physical realities.
14.name: The All-Devouring Eye

15.content: The Celestial Book is the great astral being of the understanding of magic, venerated by researchers and ritualists. Veneration: "I venerate the Celestial Book," Clive says, describing a blessing that triggered a racial gift evolution, changing the human special-attack affinity to a spell affinity, like the elves. It is "fairly common for those of us heavily involved in magical theory". Not a god of books: Jason first asks if it is "the god of books, or something". It is named among the great astral beings interested in physical realities. Approachable: its stones are described as "a lot more approachable than the Reaper". A word on proportionality: the World-Phoenix reminds the Builder, "The Celestial Book wanted me to remind you about proportionality... The ritualist is one of his", meaning Clive, and the book will not tolerate a gold-ranker sent to kill the boy out of spite.
15.name: The Celestial Book

16.content: The Keeper of Moments, also called the Keeper of the Sands, is the great astral being that governs time. Domain: "Even the Keeper of Moments, the great astral being that governs time, cannot [affect the past]".
16.name: The Keeper of Moments

17.content: Legion is the great astral being that administers the cosmic rules governing life itself. No blessings: Legion and the All-Devouring Eye are not known to hand out blessings. Domain and realm: Legion "administers the cosmic rules that govern life itself", and its realm abuts the All-Devouring Eye's region, a place "where life and annihilation are neighbours". A sanguine horror was summoned from a "nightmare realm where the Limitless Legion met the Final Domain".
17.name: Legion

18.content: The Builder is the great astral being of construction, whose work is forging universes. There have been two. The first built the twin universes of Earth and Pallimustus and was sanctioned for it. The second, the Builder of the present, is a mortal messenger who was raised to the office and whose authority is held on conditions. He is obsessed with physical reality, runs the cults that hunt astral spaces, and is building a universe of his own. Obsession and method: "obsessed with physical reality while, by its very nature, being unable to co-exist with it", the Builder recruits people to carve off the astral spaces connected to their world, then steps in and claims them. He gathers followers rather than crossing the World-Phoenix. Tools: star seeds, tokens, cults, constructs and clockwork animals. The three-way meeting: the Builder meets the Reaper and the World-Phoenix, grandly says "I will be worshipped by an entire universe... A god beyond gods", and is told that "we are the rules". The Reaper's terms bar him from interfering with Jason's birth world or producing new star seeds, tokens or vessels. In return the World-Phoenix will offer Jason a power at the cost of no further resurrections. Observers: the Builder's observer constructs accompany a group at a test, and Shade reads this as the Builder testing them.
18.name: The Builder

19.content: The Reaper is the great astral being of the finality of death. It is distinct from the god of Death of Pallimustus, who only guides souls into the astral. Its vessel is Velius. Domain: "The Reaper is very big on the finality of death. Some consider it the true god of death, as all our god of death governs is the passage of the soul into the astral". Items and orders: the Way of the Reaper is a set of skill books, and the Order of the Reaper's teachings are collected in its legacy. The Order of the Reaper used ancient knowledge of how to anchor such realms, "provided by the Reaper itself". Reaper awakening stones give mostly aggressive utility and conjuration powers. Speaking through Velius: when the Reaper takes over its vessel, the warm voice becomes "cold and bleak". It tells the Builder that Jason "carried the World-Phoenix's token. Those pacts are older than you and I will not violate them". The rules: "We are the rules. To deny them is to deny ourselves". It arranges the compromise between the Builder and the World-Phoenix and makes its own concession, because it fears being made a farce if Jason is resurrected over and over. Shade: "Of all my children, Shade has ever followed his own path", the Reaper says, with a brief fatherly smile.
19.name: The Reaper

20.content: The World-Phoenix is the great astral being of dimensional integrity: it keeps universes from tearing, and it set Jason's journey in motion. Its prime vessels are called First Servant or First Sister, and Dawn, a former vessel, is its hierophant. The mark on Jason: his first status screens carry a symbol of a fire bird, and an ability labelled "Authority of the World Phoenix". Jason says the World-Phoenix gave him "a gift as his soul passed through the astral", and that he is an outworlder through "happenstance". Its role: "the integrity of dimensions is mine. It is only with my permission that you can conduct your little game". The Builder will not cross it. The meeting of three: the World-Phoenix attends in a celestine vessel with alabaster skin and ruby hair, "a teasing smile and an amused twinkle in her red, gemstone eyes". She calls Jason "a pleasantly effective little seedling", and negotiates with the Reaper over terms that forbid the Builder from interfering with Jason's world.
20.name: The World-Phoenix

21.content: An essence ability is a power an essence user has from an essence. Each essence gives five; one is awakened at absorption and the rest are awakened later by stones. Each ability has a type, a cost, a cooldown and a rank, and gains a new effect at each rank. Four attributes, Power, Speed, Spirit and Recovery, each bond to one of the four essences and rise in rank as that essence's abilities are mastered. Abilities and attributes together decide when a person can move up a rank. Special attack (melee, drain, wounding, blood): Leech Bite. Spell (drain): Blood Harvest. Special ability (dimension, teleport): Path of Shadows. Aura (holy, unholy): Hegemony. Conjuration (darkness, light, dimension): Cloak of Night. Familiar (ritual, summon): Sanguine Horror.
21.name: Abilities and Attributes

22.content: Adventuring is the work of killing monsters and clearing hazards for pay. In practice an adventurer is a licensed contractor: they take posted notices and contracts from a jobs hall, work in a team, and are paid in spirit coins and loot. Most are not heroes in the story sense, and the profession is as much about judgement and bookkeeping as combat. This file describes how the work runs. The organisation is described in 05_Organisations/Adventure_Society.md.
22.name: The Adventuring Profession

23.content: An affliction is a condition that harms its target for a time; a boon is a condition that helps. Both are named in brackets in System messages, carry tags (poison, disease, curse, holy, unholy, magic and others) and can stack. Defence against afflictions is a game of resisting, cleansing and negating: a cleanse removes an affliction, resistance reduces the chance or strength of one landing, and some afflictions are built to defeat both. In this world a character who understands which tool beats which condition has a large tactical advantage, and Jason's power set is built around that interplay.
23.name: Afflictions, Boons and Damage

24.content: Alongside essences and stones the world has a layer of working magic that does not need an essence: quintessence gems, spirit coins, potions, ointments, enchanted tools and growth items that rise in rank. This file describes what these materials are and how they are used. It does not list individual named items; those are in 09_Items_and_Artefacts/.
24.name: Alchemy, Artifice and Magical Materials

key: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
25.comment: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
25.content: Three kinds of event reshape territory in the series. Astral spaces are pocket worlds attached to a physical world through apertures. Proto-astral spaces are short-lived, unstable versions of them that Earth suffers from. Transformation zones are sealed events that rewrite a place and the people in it. Monster surges are periodic increases in monster numbers across a world. All four are driven by the same source: raw magic leaking through from the astral.
keys: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
25.name: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges

26.content: An aura is the projection of a ranked person's soul. It grows with rank, is read by other ranked people as a sense of danger, strength and mood, and is how adventurers judge each other before words are spoken. Controlling the aura is a skill with three basic parts: projecting it, restraining it and suppressing other people's. Auras can be hidden, masked, aimed at normal people to intimidate them, and, at silver rank, begin to lift the body off the ground.
26.name: Auras

27.content: An awakening stone is a consumable crystal that awakens one essence ability the user has not yet awakened. It is the third kind of non-living magic Rufus lists, after essences and quintessence. The stone does not choose the ability; it steers toward a theme, and what comes out depends mostly on the essences the user holds. Stones are how a new essence user fills out the twenty abilities that a full set carries, and they are bought, auctioned, given as rewards and kept as family wealth.
27.name: Awakening Stones

28.content: A confluence is the fourth essence a person receives. It is not picked, bought or found. It is produced by the three essences already absorbed, and it arrives the moment the third is used. In the main run of the series a given trio of essences always gives the same confluence, and the Magic Society keeps a list of the known trios. Confluences are rated and talked about as if they were essences in their own right, and many of the best-known power sets belong to a confluence.
28.name: Confluences

29.content: Earth has the same magic as Pallimustus in a much thinner form. Through most of its history essences and monsters did not exist there at all; magic leaked in through short-lived proto-astral spaces, and a small number of secret societies used the powers that people could earn from them. When Jason returns in Book 4, Earth's magic is low and rising, with a planetary Grid of rituals monitoring and containing the leaks. The monster waves of Book 5 and the transformation zones that follow end that system.
29.name: Magic on Earth

30.content: The books name far more essences than the wiki lists give with evidence. This file collects those the text actually shows, with who holds them and what the text says of their behaviour. Rarity statements come from the text; where the text gives none, none is invented. It is intended as a quick reference for building a character's power set, not as a mechanical list. The full set of essences the Magic Society knows is in its living document. The wiki's fuller lists of essences, confluences and combinations are in../Appendices/Wiki_Reference_Lists.md, with a cross-reference to the first book line for each entry found in the text. Where the wiki gives a rarity, it agrees with the text so far: sin is Legendary, renewal is Epic and rune and vast are among the highest.
30.name: Essence Catalogue

31.content: An essence is the most powerful and rarest of the forms in which magic condenses into something that is not alive. It is absorbed into a person's soul and gives that person a set of five abilities tied to its concept. Four essences make a full set. A person with a full set becomes iron rank and is changed by it. Essences are how Pallimustus makes essence users: the people who fight monsters, serve in the churches and run most of the world's institutions.
31.name: Essences

32.content: A familiar is a creature made or called to serve one person for life. A summoned familiar is built by ritual from magical materials and a being drawn from the deep astral; a bonded familiar is a creature that answers a call. Familiars are different from the short-lived summons many essence users can conjure in the middle of a fight, and from conjurations, which are things drawn out of mana. All three are essence abilities and come from awakening stones or from the essences themselves; none can be used by anyone who lacks the necessary ritual knowledge.
32.name: Familiars, Summons and Conjurations

33.content: An essence user can grow in power in two ways. One is to consume monster cores, which is easy and can be bought. The other is to train, fight real danger and meditate. Rufus's teaching in Book 1 is that the first method eats into the potential of the second. The setting's politics, from the aristocratic families of Greenstone to the Network on Earth, turn on which method a group has used, and on what it costs them later.
33.name: Monster Cores and Training

34.content: Monsters are the most common way magic manifests in a magic-rich world. They appear from nothing, usually in the wild, live for a time that depends on their rank, and then dissolve back into raw magic if not killed first. They have ranks like essence users; the ranks are not given by essences but by the density of the magic that makes them. Hunting them before they reach their aggressive final stage is the bulk of an adventurer's work, and what they leave behind funds much of the economy.
34.name: Monsters

key: Progression Tracks: When Rank, Essence and Ability Were Gained
35.comment: Progression Tracks: When Rank, Essence and Ability Were Gained
35.content: This file records, for Jason and a few teammates, the first chapter where each rank, essence and ability appears. Jason's lines come from the system messages that announce them. For Jason's full gold-rank power set, see Jason_Power_Set_Reference.md. "First shown" means the first line the compendium found, which may come a chapter after an unreported awakening.
keys: Progression Tracks: When Rank, Essence and Ability Were Gained
35.name: Progression Tracks: When Rank, Essence and Ability Were Gained

36.content: Rank is the world's measure of power. It runs from normal people through iron, bronze, silver, gold and diamond; beyond diamond are gods and great astral beings, who are not part of the ladder. Essence users and monsters share the ladder, and each rank "has a suppressive effect on lower ranks". Rank changes the body, the length of life, what a person can do with their aura and the way other people treat them. It is the setting's class system.
36.name: Ranks and Advancement

37.content: Ritual magic is the practice of drawing a diagram, a circle with lines and glyphs, and powering it with external magic to do something an essence ability cannot. It is used for absorbing essences, awakening stones, summoning familiars, spreading wards and tracking, and, in permanent form, as formations and arrays. Ritual magic is learned, not given by an essence, and a competent ritualist is a valuable member of any team. Anyone can learn external magic; only essence users can combine it with essence powers.
37.name: Rituals, Arrays and Formations

38.content: A skill book is a consumable magical book that implants knowledge directly into the reader. It can teach a language, a martial art, the basics of ritual magic or a branch of astral magic. A skill book gives technique and information, not understanding or practice, and the people who use them well prepare beforehand and consolidate afterwards. They are the fast, flawed route to ability in a skill, in the same way that cores are the fast, flawed route to rank.
38.name: Skill Books and Learning

39.content: A soul is the part of a person that essences and ranks change. It shapes the body, projects the aura, leaves marks when wounded and, on death, lingers briefly before drifting into the astral. Healing magic can reverse a death only in that grace period and only with powerful magic. Everyday healing is done by the Healer's church, by alchemists and by healing abilities, and it is in short supply compared to demand.
39.name: Souls, Death and Healing

40.content: A title is how the System writes down a change to the soul: it appears as a window after a soul has been scarred or tested and usually changes the owner's aura. A blessing is a gift from a god or great astral being that evolves a racial gift. Titles come from what happens to a person, blessings from what a transcendent being chooses to give. The two meet in Jason's story because the same events scar his soul and attract the blessings of the World-Phoenix and the Reaper.
40.name: Titles and Blessings

41.content: Most magic in the setting follows the essence-and-rank structure described elsewhere in this folder. A smaller body of magic does not: the gifts a person is born with or earns as a race, the outworlder abilities that give Jason a game-like interface, titles drawn from soul damage, time magic, and the powers of great astral beings and gods. This file collects them so a storyteller knows what exists and who has what. It does not attempt to explain the cosmology; see 02_Cosmology_and_Powers/. Interface: the screens and System messages; "interpret reality through a recognisable medium". Quest System: quests with rewards, including a "racial gift transfiguration". Inventory: a grid of forty slots with a currency counter; items are plucked from and pushed into the screen. Astral Affinity: "Increased resistance to dimension effects and astral forces. Dimension abilities have increased effect and transcendent damage is increased". Mysterious Stranger: "Language adaptation. Essence, awakening stone and skill-book absorption. Immunity to identification and tracking effects".
41.name: Unusual and Unique Magic

42.content: Belinda is the team's trickster and utility caster: Magic, Trap and Adept, producing the Charlatan confluence. Her set borrows other people's powers, shapes herself into other roles, sets traps and teleports allies. She is delighted by her own power: "I was looking through the abilities it's known to give and they sound fantastic".
42.name: Belinda Callahan's Power Set

43.content: Clive is the team's battlemage and ritualist: Magic, Rune, Balance and the Karmic confluence. His set is built on one big spell, retributive karma effects that punish attackers, ritual circles and mana support. Spells are his focus; he uses magical weapons like staves and wands and works with his familiar.
43.name: Clive Standish's Power Set

44.content: Farrah is a volcano-themed battlemage and ritualist: Earth, Fire and Potent, which form the Volcano confluence. She fights in glossy obsidian armour with a sword that becomes a lava whip, burning orbs and lava spells, and her ritual magic underlies the team's summons and later the Grid repairs. Obsidian armour: heavy obsidian armour that glows with internal heat; a full set of glossy obsidian shards swept into wing shapes with a red glow between the segments. Sword: a huge obsidian sword whose blade is "a pillar of jagged segments" that can break up and whip around on a cord of glowing magma. Unextended it is a jagged-edge greatsword; as a whip-sword the teeth are strung on a flexible cord of red-hot lava. Lava cannon: a showstopping power that "devoured mana like pigs with a fresh corpse"; she uses it to devastate a team of silver-rankers. Orbs: three flaming orbs manifest over her head and shoot fiery beams; at the Network fight they are "searing flame" orbs. Magma and obsidian terrain: a glowing sigil on the ground produces a magma geyser, a curtain of obsidian shards from a stomp, an obsidian wall that explodes into shards, and a spike that impales. Finisher: she turns the obsidian fragments left in an enemy into lava. Magma elemental summon: a pile of black and red magma with arms, summoned from a ritual circle like Gary's golem. Ritual magic: she adjusts circles for ambient magic and teaches Emi, Hiro and others magical theory.
44.name: Farrah Hurin's Power Set

45.content: Gary is a leonid smith-warrior: hammer, fire, iron and the forge confluence. His set is a conjured suit of armour, a heavy hammer and shield, a forge golem he summons from iron filings, and forge powers for repair and alloys. Armour and weapons: conjured full-body armour of dark steel plates held together with large bolts, engraved with runes; he fights with a huge hammer and a shield. He forges a hammer himself to fight constructs. Forge golem: he pours iron filings into a circle, his hand bursts into flame, and a three-metre golem of ugly black iron rises with molten metal between the joints. The text calls it a foundry golem when he names it and a forge golem later. It is a temporary summon, unlike a familiar. Summoning powers need ritual understanding, as for Farrah. Forge powers: he uses a forge essence power to repair a wagon wheel, and creates "alloys heavier and stronger than steel" for the academy annex. Smithing: he forges Jason's Dread Salvation. Rescue work: in the Book 9 surge he and other craftspeople shape stone and reinforce structures, and his golem's chest plate opens to carry survivors.
45.name: Gary's Power Set

46.content: Humphrey is the team's heavy hitter: "simple, reliable power". His dragon, wing and might essences give him a dragon-winged flyer with fire, a weapon-heavy attack set and racial gifts that scale with risk. His familiar is the mirage dragon Stash.
46.name: Humphrey Geller's Power Set

47.content: Neil is the team's healer and shield-caster: Shield, Growth and Renewal, producing the Prosperity confluence. His set is built around timed, short-lived shields, buffs on allies and ritual healing, and Prosperity luck effects. Rufus is struck by the shielding: the shields "lasted only moments and would end after absorbing only a single attack", so they need good judgement and timing.
47.name: Neil Davone's Power Set

48.content: Rufus is a swordsman-teleporter built on the sun and moon: a skilled fighter whose powers blend movement, teleportation, illusory after-images and attacks. In the Greenstone years he fights as a bronze-ranker with a golden and a silver sword; by Book 9 his essence is described as the eclipse confluence, and his combat shifts between sun, moon and eclipse states. Conjured swords: a golden sword and a silver sword that appear in his hand. The swords leave marks: those cut by the golden sword have a small orb of fire, "a miniature golden sun", floating around them and scorching them; those touched by the silver sword have a tiny moon that soaks up heat instead. Speed of light: when he activates it "the world seemed to freeze in time around him", giving "only two seconds of accelerated time"; the text calls it "one of his strongest trump cards". Movement chain: unlike Jason, he does not have one teleport he can use over and over; "he had a slew of powers that blended movement, teleportation, illusionary after-images and attacks" and chaining them takes skill and practice. Water-walking boots are noted in his character file. Kingdom of Eclipse: his incantation-driven power, whose chant ends "bring forth the kingdom of eclipse"; it fires an eclipse orb that kills dozens.
48.name: Rufus Remore's Power Set

49.content: Sophie is a skill-based speed fighter: a celestine whose Swift, Balance and Wind essences form the Mystic confluence. Her set stacks movement, perception and unarmed techniques around one idea, acting faster and more precisely than the enemy. Before Jason's help she had only the Swift essence and its single ability for more than half a dozen years.
49.name: Sophie Wexler's Power Set

key: Calendar, Holidays, Naming Customs and Forms of Address
50.comment: Calendar, Holidays, Naming Customs and Forms of Address
50.content: The Pallimustus calendar is close to Earth's but not the same: twelve months of thirty days, five extra days and a six-day week with simple day names. Naming customs and forms of address mark rank, family and role, and Rimaros has a distinctive palindrome custom for prominent adults.
keys: Calendar, Holidays, Naming Customs and Forms of Address
50.name: Calendar, Holidays, Naming Customs and Forms of Address

51.content: Metallic-haired, metallic-eyed people with an astral affinity, produced when two outworlders have a child. Appearance: Sophie has chocolate skin and shining silver hair, her eyes matching it exactly, "the matching metallics a giveaway trait of the celestine race". In Kurdansk many celestines have dark skin and silver hair. Astral affinity: astral affinity is a celestine racial gift; celestines are similar to elves and humans. The rare Child of the Celestial Wind appears only in races with astral affinity, on Pallimustus meaning celestines, or potentially outworlders. Origin: Dawn says two outworlders who have a child produce a celestine, and celestines propagate with their own kind; she is herself a child of two outworlders. Gift evolutions: Sophie's Mana Integrity becomes Mana Wellspring, her Astral Affinity becomes Boundary Breaker and her Celestial Swiftness becomes Princess of the Firmament. Communities: Zartos is a subterranean city largely populated by celestines. Messengers: messengers are about half again as tall as a celestine, and their servants take care never to imply the resemblance. Dawn's true form: a celestine with ruby eyes and hair.
51.name: Celestines

key: Clothing, Food, Festivals and Transport by Region
52.comment: Clothing, Food, Festivals and Transport by Region
52.content: A regional table of how people dress, eat, celebrate and travel. Daily_Life.md covers Greenstone and the delta in detail; this file adds Rimaros and the Storm Kingdom, Yaresh, Kurdansk, Pranay, Vitesse and smaller places, and gathers the festivals the text names.
keys: Clothing, Food, Festivals and Transport by Region
52.name: Clothing, Food, Festivals and Transport by Region

key: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
53.comment: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
53.content: The practical texture of life in Greenstone and the delta: the calendar, what people wear and eat, how they travel and what runs on spirit coins. Calendar: "twelve months of thirty days, divided up into early, mid and late stages of each season", five extra days for the solstices, equinoxes and the new year, which falls at the beginning of spring. The week has six days. Clothing: "Most people, whether in Greenstone or the delta, wore loose-fitting, breathable clothes because of the heat"; adventurers on a job wear fitted outfits, often with protective properties. Elf fashion has flowing, tapered lines. Food: preparation is often familiar, with bread, soup, sandwiches and cake, but the ingredients are mostly different because farms raise different animals and trees bear different fruit. Jason lists local sauce ingredients with a village cook. Housing: Leust, one of the delta's largest towns, has paved roads and stone buildings "instead of mud-brick"; in the Island, green stone appears everywhere. Transport: heidels are "the size and shape of a horse, but with scales instead of hair and two heads, each with a horn"; the Island's districts are linked by a subterranean, submarine transit line called the loop, with terminals laid out like train stations. Devices: lamps, showers and most household magic run on lesser spirit coins.
keys: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
53.name: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport

54.content: Large, scaled humanoids who claim descent from dragons and whose homeland is the Dragon Lands. Appearance: "a member of the rare draconian race, larger even than male leonids and covered in glossy scales", the colour of dark leaves, green moving into purple; Maximilian is the tallest person in Greenstone, with a long hairless head and glossy scales. A draconian skull is distinctive enough to identify skeletons. Pride in descent: draconians "took pride in their claimed dragon ancestry and often had issues with other races wielding the dragon essence". Homeland: the Dragon Lands, Pallimustus's version of Antarctica, "the native land of the large, scaled humanoids known as draconians", with active volcanoes, hot springs and "dragon mouth" geysers from subterranean apertures to a realm of fire. Rarity: draconians are rare in Greenstone, where Maximilian is the only one present at a gathering.
54.name: Draconians

55.content: Dreisil is the nation of Kurdansk, Sophie's birthplace. The text names it once and gives its full title. Kurdansk_Culture.md covers the life of the city and is the main file for what is known of the nation's people. Name: Kurdansk lies "in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil". Humphrey's view: "The more they try to make a nation sound free and righteous, the more tyrannical and corrupt it is". Prisons: Kurdansk uses prisons rather than indenture as punishment.
55.name: Dreisil: The People's Holy Federation

56.content: How money works on Pallimustus: spirit coins in six denominations that also power devices and sustain essence users, farms that make them, and who controls them. Denominations: "The basic coin of the realm was the lesser spirit coin. Iron spirit coins were worth a hundred lesser coins, used by bulk traders, adventurers and other members of the wealthy elite. After that, it was ten iron to the bronze, ten bronze to the silver and ten silver to the gold"; three gold coins are "worth three hundred thousand units of the basic currency". Why the lesser coin is the basic unit: higher-rank coins are "not very useful for everyday life"; almost all home and business magic devices, such as lamps and showers, run on lesser coins and higher ranks would burn them out, while larger infrastructure such as the loop line uses more powerful coins. Sustenance: ranked people can live on spirit coins; Rufus says a bronze coin will sustain bronze-rank adventurers without stressing their bodies, so it is about not going over your limit. Farms: spirit coins are made on farms using special moulds that cause magic to crystallise, in delicate, very stable ambient magic.
56.name: Economy and Money

57.content: Elves are powerful spellcasters whose healing magic is unparalleled. Reputation: "Elves are powerful spell casters and their skill with healing magic is unparalleled". Aptitude: the elven aptitude is for spells rather than the special attacks humans favour. Racial gift: Neil's elf racial ability, Life Affinity, evolves into Life Guard. Local families: Greenstone has local elf families; Lucian Lamprey is an elf banished there who is not one of them, and Pochard Finn is an elf and a local. Elf fashion: "flowing, tapered lines". Notable elves: Allayeth and Charist, Yaresh's two diamond-rank elves; Hana Shavar, High Priestess of the Healer; Elspeth Arella, director of the Greenstone Adventure Society. Predation: cannibals in Book 1 discuss elves as food.
57.name: Elves

key: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
58.comment: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
58.content: A large, densely populated kingdom of old noble houses, garden towers and high-magic farmland, and the homeland from which Greenstone was colonised. Standing: "One of the most prominent kingdoms in the world" with a royal family; the Queen of Estercost and other members of its elite ask Jason to arbitrate over the System's withdrawal. Population: a "large and densely populated kingdom" and the land from which Greenstone was colonised centuries earlier; the region is "filled with towns, villages and smaller cities, due to the idyllic climate and rich natural resources". Capital and councils: Cyrion is the capital, yet the Adventure Society's continental council sits in Vitesse, where the royal family keeps a tower as a palace; in Book 7 the Cyrion branch takes over the site of the operation from Vitesse. Vitesse: the city of flowers, on what Jason would know as the French Riviera, with garden towers that house the wealthy elite and key organisations. Adventurers think of it as the continent's adventuring capital, because its high magic spawns powerful, frequent monster manifestations. Aristocracy: the Remore family has no title, while the Gellers hold only the title from their small provincial city of origin and refuse all others; neither is begrudged a premier tower. Cyrion's laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families". House Headingway is "one of Estercost's pre-eminent families".
keys: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
58.name: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats

key: Girlano: Culture of a Cartel Kingdom
59.comment: Girlano: Culture of a Cartel Kingdom
59.content: Girlano is an inland nation south of the Storm Kingdom, ostensibly a kingdom but controlled by cartels that produce banned or heavily controlled substances. It has a reputation, and the text shows it only through reputation and a border city. Rule: "ostensibly a kingdom", it is "famously controlled by cartels known for producing substances that ranged from heavily controlled to outright banned"; the cartels keep power through under-the-table deals with powerful groups in neighbouring countries, which prop up a puppet government while their own governments pay lip service to suppression. Economy: the cartels exploit the region's rare plants and minerals, and the nation is surrounded by strong public sanctions and border controls. Smuggling culture: the border with the Storm Kingdom is jungle-covered hills with many semi-hidden smuggling paths to the shore. The border city Casallini is a small city where the Adventure Society keeps a large force because it is a border city. Neutral Society: the Adventure Society ignores borders and politics and keeps monsters out of population centres, so long as its work is not interfered with. Reputation: Liara calls it "a stain full of drug dealers and smugglers". Belinda finds it "famously sketchy" with "all the opportunities it offered to an enterprising and open-minded young lady". Hired muscle: the men who attack Sophie's delivery are local hires from Casallini.
keys: Girlano: Culture of a Cartel Kingdom
59.name: Girlano: Culture of a Cartel Kingdom

60.content: Goblins and fairies appear as monsters and as people of Earth transformed by the zones; fairies are also a small hovering manifestation. Goblins as monsters: Jason jokes about killing ten goblins for an uncommon spear in the cannibals' cave. Transformed humans: in West Canfield, Detroit, people were "turned into goblins and their homes into underground warrens", which became a lawless combat zone. Cabal beings: the Cabal's mythological beings include centaurs, ogres, fairies and more. Elves, goblins and fairies: people in a magic city were "turned into elves and goblins and fairies". Fairy manifestation: a small hovering fairy-like figure with an androgynous body bites Clive in Book 2. Earth beings in the open: as the Cabal operated in the open, "centaurs, ogres, fairies, and more" were spotted by the media and revealed to the world. A Network operative expects the Cabal to be "myths and fairy tale creatures". Zone-turned people: Emi says people in a magic city "were all turned into elves and goblins and fairies", so they were let live there. Jason's cloud city is described as a fairy tale kingdom, but that is a style, not a people.
60.name: Goblins and Fairies: Zone-Transformed Peoples

61.content: The most common people of Pallimustus and Earth's native people, with gifts that favour special attacks and fast essence advancement. Racial gifts: an affinity for special attacks, essences that advance more rapidly than others', and latent powers that adapt to the essences. The latent gifts are dormant until awakened and then take a form based on the person's essences. Evolution: Clive's blessing from the Celestial Book changes his human special attack affinity into a spell affinity; his Human Ambition becomes Thirst for Knowledge and Humphrey's Special Attack Affinity becomes Attack of the Mirage Dragon. Taika's human abilities have been replaced with outworlder ones. Distribution: the Greenstone region is human-dominated. Humans and outworlders: an outworlder who has a child with another species produces offspring of that species, so a human and an outworlder have a human child. Lifespan: essence users age slower; bronze-rankers can live well past a hundred, silvers double that and gold-rankers live for centuries.
61.name: Humans

key: Jayapura: Culture of a Pranay Trade Port
62.comment: Jayapura: Culture of a Pranay Trade Port
62.content: Jayapura is a northern-coast sea-trade port of Pranay and the birthplace of Hester. Pranay_Culture.md covers the land; this file gives Jayapura's own life: the mirage arenas as entertainment, floating discs, markets and the Mystic Quarter. Trade port: one of the important sea-trade ports on Pranay's northern coast. Arena culture: its mirage chamber complex is the city's premier entertainment venue, with essence users facing each other or illusion challenges before a paying audience. "There are whole essence user teams who never become adventurers"; they earn money in the arena and use monster cores to rank. Two leagues a year in silver, bronze and iron divisions lead to grand championships. See Mirage_Chamber_Association.md. Retirement: arena professionals stop using cores before gold, retire when silver longevity runs out and become gold-rank managers of the arena. Layout: a flat circular arena building at the edge of the Mystic Quarter, spilling into the theatre district. Transport: those who can afford them ride platter-sized floating discs; floating discs are sold in the Mystic Quarter. Markets and food: the team visits its markets and finds new customs and food. A nondescript tattoo parlour run by Tilly is where Jason gets his crest. Ice cream: Jason remembers kulfi-like ice cream from there.
keys: Jayapura: Culture of a Pranay Trade Port
62.name: Jayapura: Culture of a Pranay Trade Port

key: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
63.comment: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
63.content: A river city in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil, where celestines with dark skin and silver hair are common, entertainment and crime share the old docks, and prisons rather than indenture punish crime. Nation: Kurdansk lies "in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil". Celestines: "Like many of Kurdansk's celestines, she had dark skin and silver hair", and the rowhouses are narrow and wedged together. Entertainment quarter: a former warehouse district near the Kurdan River docks, now the most viable site for large theatre halls, "a heady mix of pleasure, criminality and money". Skyport: it has a busy skyport with towers where airships dock. The Reaper link: Melody Jain's story begins in Kurdansk around twenty-five years before Book 9.
keys: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
63.name: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil

64.content: ; Indenture, not slavery: "We don't have slaves. We have indentured servants. A lot of criminals are sentenced to indenture, then their indenture is sold or auctioned to recoup the cost of their crimes". Jason finds the system disturbing and says both his world and this one need better systems. Captured enemies: the Ustei do not accept slavery; "their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death". The Adventure Society agreement: a clause in the Adventure Society's agreement with Greenstone gives anyone who completes a contract the right of refusal on anyone sentenced to indenture as a result of it. Hearings: indenture hearings are a normal legal event; the Greenstone court "was less like an American legal p[roceeding]". House guards: in Cyrion, house guards are "technically a form of indentured servitude" and the laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families". Jason's argument: if a family used "draconian measures" to hold people to cheap work, nothing would stop them. The System's withdrawal: the System will withdraw access "in regions of Pallimustus currently operating with slavery, indentured servitude or similar legal systems". "The Queen of Estercost and several other interested parties" ask for arbitration over the withdrawal. Slave markets: Jason's friend scouts Sadi Andali's slave markets, and Ben asks whether "the destruction of the Sadi Andali slave trade" is Jason's price.
64.name: Law and Indenture

65.content: Lion-headed, furred, strong and fast people; Gary is the best-known leonid. Strength and stamina: "Members of his leonid race are stronger and faster than us, and that's only the beginning of what leonids can do"; a leonid needs far more exertion than others to tire, another racial gift. Appearance: a huge "lion man" whose voice is growly by default; Gary is "so huge he made bodybuilders look like they w[ere small]". He is covered in fur. Size: draconians are larger even than male leonids. Mixed company: a leonid, an elf and a celestine are among the eleven people who emerge from Dawn's cottage in Book 7.
65.name: Leonids

66.content: Merfolk are named once in the books as people, not fish; no detail beyond that is established here. Only reference: Emir answers a joke about someone's partner ("Man, woman or fish?") with "Merfolk are not fish. They happen to be very sensual people". Open gap: no chapter text found so far gives merfolk appearance, homeland or gifts.
66.name: Merfolk

key: The Mirror Kingdom: Culture of a Kingdom Ruled by a Diamond-Ranker
67.comment: The Mirror Kingdom: Culture of a Kingdom Ruled by a Diamond-Ranker
67.content: The Mirror Kingdom, also called the Kingdom of Mirrors, is a small, affluent kingdom founded and ruled for more than eight centuries by a diamond-ranker, the Mirror King. Its princes and princesses are many, and its prince Valdis leads an adventuring team in Greenstone. Nature: "the diminutive but influential Kingdom of Mirrors. Small, affluent and geographically blessed, it had neither expanded its borders nor been had its borders encroached upon in more than eight centuries". The king: the diamond-ranker known as the Mirror King founded the kingdom and rules it still; he has had "a series of queens, reportedly doting on each, even as they grew old and died beside him", and Valdis is one of the current queen consort's sons. Court manners: kneeling is expected before the king; his protocol officer Hastor tells Jason "You should kneel", and the king says Hastor "starts getting snippy" without a seating chart by rank. Valdis's team drops to one knee on the king's arrival. The king is amused, warm and teasing with his son. Teams built around princes: Valdis's team was built around him, "the shaft to his spearhead". The kingdom has its own battles with the Builder cult. The king's aura: Jason, an iron-ranker, finds the king's aura felt like part of the world, "in perfect symbiosis with the world", and it later inspires his own aura control. Portals: the king has his own portal specialist, Hastor, who calls up a glass-like portal.
keys: The Mirror Kingdom: Culture of a Kingdom Ruled by a Diamond-Ranker
67.name: The Mirror Kingdom: Culture of a Kingdom Ruled by a Diamond-Ranker

68.content: People whose souls re-entered a physical reality, manifesting a new body; they carry unusual gifts and cannot be easily tracked. Definition: Clive: "An outworlder is someone whose soul has re-entered a physical reality, reflexively manifesting a body for itself"; the body is "akin to that of a monster, or a summoned familiar", physical substance forged from raw magic, between the astral and the physical. How it happens: natural magical phenomena connecting two realities drag someone through; their body is annihilated in the astral and their soul reconstitutes one. Advantages: Farrah says outworlders "might have their advantages", and Jason's abilities (map, interface, astral affinity) are outworlder abilities. Children: an outworlder with another species produces offspring of that species; two outworlders produce a celestine. Arrivals: a hundred and nineteen outworlders arrive at once in Book 7; two outworlders among the eleven people in Dawn's cottage are bronze rank.
68.name: Outworlders

key: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
69.comment: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
69.content: The large southern land corresponding to Sri Lanka, where portal stopovers and isolated city-states form a trading hub, and where Jayapura is the port Hester calls home. Geography: Pranay is this world's equivalent of Sri Lanka, "larger and further south", a huge landmass in the Indian Ocean. Its northern coast has several important sea-trade connections in a world without the Arabian Peninsula. Jayapura: Hester's birth city; personal transport for those who can afford it is a platter-sized floating disc ridden by shifting weight. Mirage chambers: Jayapura has a vast mirage chamber complex, more sophisticated than the Gellers' private chamber in Greenstone because the higher magic allows potent dimensional magic and concurrent chambers. Massive city: Jason's team visited Pranay's urban centre after their first Reaper astral space and saw only familiars as magical beasts.
keys: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
69.name: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States

70.content: How faith appears day to day: crowded temple districts with hierarchies of their own, churches that serve as hospitals and archives, and gods whose rules limit what they can do. Temple districts: temples line the road to the Island's Divine Square and "gods had hierarchies of their own": the Temple of Roads sits behind the larger Temple of Journeys. The square is crowded with booths selling religious paraphernalia and people proselytising. Dominion: "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles. It is he who determines who rules, and who serves". The Healer: Neil makes a stand in the Temple of the Healer; ex-clergy who offended their gods and were stripped of divinely gifted essences suffer a debilitating imbalance in body and soul; the notes make the Healer the god who does this. Knowledge's temple: in Rimaros it is "an important resource for the many magical researchers" with a symbiotic relationship with the Magic Society branch; the temple is mostly a vast library covering multiple wings. Churches and research: churches, especially Knowledge's, help fund the Magical Research Association. Death's paperwork: the Church of Death issues certification of how many times a person has died. Limits on gods: a god's favour does not mean intervention; a goddess says she cannot see into the astral space where Jason holds prisoners; the gods are "bound by convoluted limitations".
70.name: Religion in Practice

71.content: Short, stocky, hairless people with deep-blue skin and naturally glowing runes. Appearance: "short and stocky, with skin of such a deep blue it was almost black", no hair and covered in faintly glowing, tattoo-like markings that are natural to the race. Rarity: they are "a rarity in Greenstone"; a runic barman in Old City is stocky and hairless with blue-black skin and glowing runes. Bones: the runes show faintly on their bones; a short, broad skeleton in the desert astral space is identified as a runic by them. Notable: Arash, a runic Jason meets in the temple district, explains Dominion's role: "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles". Part of the civilisation-building species: the list of species that build civilisations is "humans, elves and leonids, celestines, runic, smoulder and draconians". Common in Old City: a runic works as a barman, and a runic man appears at Jory's clinic. Inherent markings: the glowing runes "looked like magic tattoos but were an inherent trait". Spellcasters: "Elves and runics were the most common affliction wielders, as their predilection for spells made a ranged power set much more likely". Earth zones: when zones turn Earth people into other species, Jason, Farrah and Dawn spot elves and "the dark-skinned runic people". A runic woman appears with Rick Mercer's team. Kinship with smoulders: "Smoulders and the runic were quite similar, with their dark skin and glowing features".
71.name: Runics

72.content: Dark-skinned people with glowing red eyes and affinities for earth and fire; the brighthearts are the smoulder of the deep underground realm of Cardinas. Smoulder: "They have natural affinities for earth and fire"; a smoulder friend of Humphrey's parents has the wind essence and his earth affinity evolved into an air affinity. Niko, a member of Beth's team, has dark skin, glowing red eyes and jet-black hair. Marla is a fire aspect with skin markings, eyes and hair the yellow-orange of steel in a forge; Lorenn, an ash aspect, has smoky greys. War form: Beaufort prefers his fifteen-foot metal skeleton "war form" but must meet the brightheart smoulders in a form they will accept. Home: the largest chamber of the underground realm was home to most brightheart smoulders.
72.name: Smoulder and Brighthearts

key: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
73.comment: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
73.content: A sea kingdom ruled from Rimaros, where a gold-rank monarch rules, heirs prove themselves as adventurers, and sky islands house the cream of society. Extent: "It rules the Sea of Storms, all the islands on it and all the coastal regions that surround it"; the capital is Rimaros. Sky islands: reserved for "the cream of society": big-name adventurers, long-standing adventuring families and aristocrats; a family known for producing good adventurers is mostly inducted into the nobility, and a house without good adventurers sinks into obscurity. Monarchy: the Storm King is a gold-ranker, which one must be to take the throne; royals are not raised on cores as in most nations, since that disqualifies them here, and potential heirs from every branch are adventurers proving themselves in monster fighting and statecraft in a decades-long contest until the monarch chooses an heir. Titles: the firstborn daughter of the Storm King, if competing, is the Hurricane Princess and the firstborn son the Storm Prince; many royals bow out, often adopting into their non-royal parent's family. Palindromic names: first and last names that are palindromes are assigned in adulthood and mark important family members; the more prominent the family, the rarer the practice, and the royal family shares a name with the capital. Royal looks: the royal family's iconic feature is sapphire hair and eyes.
keys: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
73.name: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms

74.content: A nomad tribe from a region to the north that raids spirit coin convoys in the Greenstone desert and will not accept captured warriors as slaves. Who they are: the "sand pirates" are actually the Ustei Tribe, nomads from a region to the north; Humphrey identifies them as northerners from their hair and clothes. The raids: an expedition is formed to find out why they are so far south and stop them raiding spirit coin shipments. The response: the best outcome is a peaceful return north or an agreement not to attack convoys; failing that, they are to be captured and interrogated. Vincent expects them to talk if shown strength. Captives: "Their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death".
74.name: The Ustei: Northern Nomad Tribe

key: The Ustei Homeland and the Ustei Way of Life
75.comment: The Ustei Homeland and the Ustei Way of Life
75.content: The Ustei are nomads from a region to the north of Greenstone, living on oases connected to an astral space and moving with their war barge. Ustei.md covers who they are; this file collects what the text says of their homeland and customs. The homeland: a region to the north of the Greenstone desert, whose oases are connected to the astral space that supplies the desert. When the astral space's water supply failed, the oases "were no longer able to support all the nomad tribes". Travel: the entire tribe lives on a war barge, "easily the equal of a passenger liner", built on giant bones with multiple decks. See Desert_Transport_Skimmers_and_Barges.md. Warriors and ranks: only a fraction of the warriors are iron-rankers, most have one or two essences; bronze-rank captains lead them, and a silver-rank tribal chief commands the tribe. Dress: Humphrey identifies them as northerners "from the hair and clothes". Women, children and slaves: the tribe's women and children were locked away in conditions like slaves, and actual slaves were found in the same conditions. Someone floated the idea of taking the Ustei men as slaves, "which would at least be something they understood". Law of surrender: "Their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death". After defeat, they claim the barge and everything in it, including the women, children and slaves, belongs to the victor; "the idea is that now they have to go raiding for more women".
keys: The Ustei Homeland and the Ustei Way of Life
75.name: The Ustei Homeland and the Ustei Way of Life

76.content: A skinny, chihuahua-headed species that is not native to Pallimustus; humans are turned into valash by Earth's transformation zones. Origin: Jason had only seen valash when Earth's transformation zones turned humans into them; they are "a skinny sapient species not native to Pallimustus". Appearance: "skinny bodies and Chihuahua-like heads", shorter than Jason. Outworlders: the valash Jason meets in Yaresh is an outworlder with a silver-rank aura and no sign of core use. Fashion: his fitted white suit is not in the local style and "would have been more at home in a Miami nightclub in the eighties". Zolit Kreen: the valash outworlder introduces himself as "Zolit. Zolit Kreen". He was originally a valash, "attention-grabbing" for being an outworlder and a chihuahua-headed species, and "had spent years working very hard to undo that damage". A niche: he ranked to silver while staying as unremarkable as possible, then retired to be a fight promoter, where "everyone was a little bit strange" and "being a valash outworlder was his" gimmick. Prison: Adventure Society enforcers lock him up after he meets another outworlder, asking about his assistant Benella and messengers. Social standing: despite his small stature he is "not pushed, shoved, or disrespected" in a crowd, with a silver-rank aura.
76.name: Valash

key: Vitesse: Culture of the City of Flowers
77.comment: Vitesse: Culture of the City of Flowers
77.content: Vitesse is the garden-tower city of Estercost: wealthy, prosperous and full of powerful adventurers, with the Remore Academy and the continent's adventuring elite. This file covers how its people live; the geography is in../06_Places/Vitesse.md. The city of flowers: it is "known as the city of flowers", in what Jason would know as the French Riviera, with garden towers that have every third or fourth floor given to gardens "using water, light and plant magic to create lush refuges of peace". The towers house the wealthy elite, aristocrats and adventurers, and the headquarters of key organisations. Standing of the great families: the Remore family has no aristocratic title and the Gellers only a small provincial one, and neither is begrudged residences in premier towers. Adventuring: iron-rankers there may not hunt alone, because of the high magic.
keys: Vitesse: Culture of the City of Flowers
77.name: Vitesse: Culture of the City of Flowers

key: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
78.comment: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
78.content: A small-population city that grows around its trees, whose civic government is weaker than its churches and societies, and whose two elf diamond-rankers dominate its adventuring scene. Size and design: only a few tens of thousands live there, but the design accommodates the environment so that the city has the footprint of a much larger centre. Walls and gates: its walls are a line of massive trees with glossy black stone filling the gaps, tunnels pass through the trunks, and vehicles queue at a gate for inspection. Streets: alleys are nicer than the norm and resemble gardens, with gravel paths through long grass. Government: "In Yaresh, the civic administration is considerably weaker than the churches and the major societies", because one group undermines the Duke for its own ends. The Aristocratic Faction: wealthy aristocrats and a few merchant barons who own most of the land and provide most of the jobs, and who use that power to shape their tenants' ideology. They have no adventurers or researchers behind them, just money and political influence. Diamond-rankers: Allayeth and Charist, both elves; Yaresh has "not just one but two resident diamond-rankers", with Charist the more social and Allayeth the more reclusive, who raised the all-woman team Moon's Edge, led by Miriam Vance.
keys: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
78.name: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City

key: Zartos: Culture of a Celestine City Under the Earth
79.comment: Zartos: Culture of a Celestine City Under the Earth
79.content: Zartos is a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines and home to the diamond-ranker Virid, Gary's mentor. The text shows it only as a place to work and rest. Setting: "a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines". Celestine community: Gary says "Zartos has a large celestine community"; Rufus has not been, though his brother recommended it. See Celestines.md for the people. Craft: Virid keeps a personal smithy there, "the best place to forge a great work". Gary and Virid forge while the team rests.
keys: Zartos: Culture of a Celestine City Under the Earth
79.name: Zartos: Culture of a Celestine City Under the Earth

80.content: The Adventure Society is one of the three great organisations of Pallimustus. Its main purpose is monster extermination: it posts notices, issues contracts, assesses and registers adventurers, and keeps records of their kills. Its insignia is a sword and rod crossed over a shield, stitched on its staff's clothing and embossed on its badges. Restricted essences: Rufus says Death is restricted by itself, and the Magic Society's living document shows one restricted combination, the Succubus essence, which takes two insanely rare essences. A corrupt essence is on the list: a Magic-Society-bound adventurer hands one looted from an elemental to the Adventure Society "since it was on the restricted list"; the Society offers good trades for restricted essences. The wiki's fuller list and its Sacrifice-confluence pit fighter were not found in the text. Neutrality: the Society is described as neutral in disputes between nations. Corruption and reform: Rufus says there "may be some level of corruption in this branch" in Book 1; a later corruption enquiry at the Greenstone branch led to blanket demotions of two- and three-star members, who were bumped back up afterwards.
80.name: The Adventure Society

81.content: The Alchemy Association is the guild of Pallimustus' alchemists. It lends its name to the potions and salves sold in a city, sits just behind the Adventure Society and the Magic Society in a city's guild district, and wants anything that advances alchemy, from Neil's miracle potion recipe to research in Yaresh. The text never describes its ranks or leadership. Branding: a tin of salve Jason buys in Book 1 is labelled "Greenstone Alchemy Association". Membership: Jory is "a member of the Adventure Society and the Alchemist Association". Belinda says the same of another person, "in the Alchemy Association and the Adventure Society". Dual membership is ordinary. Standing: in Greenstone's guild district the Forge Society and the Alchemist Association are "clearly second to the Adventure and Magic Societies, but still occupied impressive chunks of real estate". Assistants: Jason is told he could get assistants from the Association. Interest in recipes: the Association has been "hounding" Neil for the miracle potion recipe. Benefits: organisational benefits from the Adventure Society, Magic Society, Alchemy Association "and the like" are what the top guilds care about, not material rewards. Brokered supply: a lord brokered the sale of a crate of potions through the Association, and stock runs short until people get their next batches from the vats.
81.name: The Alchemy Association

82.content: Four hidden organisations run through the books. The Order of the Reaper is an ancient order of assassins that churches destroyed. The Builder cult serves a great astral being and uses star seeds and clockwork cores. The Church of Undeath serves the corruption of the cycle itself.
82.name: Cults and Orders

key: Earth's Powers: the Network, the Cabal, the EOA and the Asano Clan
83.comment: Earth's Powers: the Network, the Cabal, the EOA and the Asano Clan
83.content: Earth has three old magical powers and, from Book 5 on, a fourth. The Network uses essence magic, the Cabal is older and tied to vampires and "old magic", and the Engineers of Ascension (EOA) is a radical group with a secret agenda. The Asano clan is Jason's family turned into a faction. Governments and the United Nations become players when magic is made public.
keys: Earth's Powers: the Network, the Cabal, the EOA and the Asano Clan
83.name: Earth's Powers: the Network, the Cabal, the EOA and the Asano Clan

84.content: The Engineers of Ascension (EOA, also written EoA) is the youngest and weakest of Earth's three old powers: a union of outsider groups that tried to engineer a higher form of humanity and prepare for the day magic became public. Four "cardinals" ran it under Mr North, and its sabotage of the Grid ended the secrecy of magic and ended the organisation. Earth_Powers.md covers it briefly; this file is the full account.
84.name: The Engineers of Ascension

85.content: A guild is an adventuring organisation that recruits, trains and backs its members and takes on a share of the Adventure Society's work. Guilds carry weight in the Society's surge quotas and in politics. Great families have their own guilds or schools; some local powers (the Aristocratic Faction) deliberately avoid personal power.
85.name: Guilds, Houses and Local Powers

key: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
86.comment: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
86.content: The Magic Society records and regulates magic: it keeps the register of essences and their combinations, oversees spirit coin farms, runs communication networks and hoards research. The Alchemy Association and the Artifice Association are the guilds of the potion-makers and of the item-makers. The living document: a marble-and-gold tablet, connected to a central record, that updates as the record changes and holds the full list of every essence and essence combination known to the Society. It is how Farrah and Rufus look up what a combination will produce. Water link: the Society's chambers allow conversation at a distance. See../03_Magic_and_Adventuring/Alchemy_Artifice_and_Magical_Materials.md (communication). Spirit coin farms: registered farms exist. The Adventure Society treats anything touching the farms as three-star work. Greenstone branch: directed by Lucian Lamprey, who uses the Fortress as his office; his deputy director Pochard Finn is an elf and a local who runs the city campus and is "the de facto director of Greenstone's Magic Society". Pochard is Clive's boss. I haven't been deputy director for several years".
keys: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
86.name: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA

87.content: The Mirage Chamber Association is the body that owns and runs the mirage chamber complex in Jayapura, the biggest such facility the books show. A mirage chamber projects illusions that feel real to those inside; the Association turns that into a training service and a league sport, and it is powerful in its city for it. It is the only named body for mirage chambers; the Geller family's private chamber in Greenstone is not part of it.
87.name: The Mirage Chamber Association

key: The Order and the Cult of the Reaper
88.comment: The Order and the Cult of the Reaper
88.content: Two different bodies carry the Reaper's name. The Cult of the Reaper is the old body of worshippers of the great astral being called the Reaper, who venerate "the finality of death" and work alongside the Church of Death. The Order of the Reaper is a faction that split from the cult to become assassins and political power-brokers, was "destroyed" by a coalition of churches, and has quietly returned. Cults_and_Orders.md holds the short entries; this file is the full account.
keys: The Order and the Cult of the Reaper
88.name: The Order and the Cult of the Reaper

89.content: The Cabal is the oldest of Earth's three dominant magical forces: a loose collection of factions of vampires, fae and other creatures older than recorded history, with old money and old habits.
