It split when ancient vampires were woken and the vampire lords rose. Part of it sides with humanity and, in the end, is openly led by Boris Ket Lundi. Earth_Powers.md covers it briefly; this file is the full account.
89.name: The Cabal

90.content: The Network is Earth's largest magical organisation: a federation of old secret societies, now national and city branches, that uses essence magic, controls most of the world's spirit coin supply, and maintains the Grid that finds and contains incursions. It went public as the Global Defense Network when the monster waves began, and later fractured into four blocs. Earth_Powers.md covers it beside the other factions; this file is the full account.
90.name: The Network

91.content: The church of Death is the Pallimustus institution for the passage of the dead: it certifies who has died and returned, helps with registration, and has long watched against necromancy. It works alongside the Cult of the Reaper, which serves as its hidden dagger.
91.name: The Church of Death

92.content: The church of Dominion is the church of rulership and the exercise of authority. It is the outlier among churches in keeping low-ranking essence users under its thumb. The god is often seen; his priests rarely are. Temple: in Greenstone it is "the strange temple" on the Divine Square, called the temple of Dominion. Control of clergy: other churches make little call on adventuring clergy; Dominion's is the most prominent outlier in keeping low-ranking essence users under its thumb. Absent priests: a character thought power and control were the church's remit, but has "never even met a priest of Dominion". The god's description: Dominion tells Jason he is "oppression-friendly", not an oppressor.
92.name: The Church of Dominion

93.content: The church of Knowledge keeps the libraries, checks the assessments and has its acolytes at hand where information matters. From Book 7 it is also quietly building a fighting force across the world, which at the end of Book 9 stops hiding.
93.name: The Church of Knowledge

key: The Church of Purity and the Lasalle Family
94.comment: The Church of Purity and the Lasalle Family
94.content: The church of Purity is the church of cleansing: it supplies the healers who treat curses and taint, and it first developed the techniques for removing star seeds. In Book 3 its leadership vanishes when its involvement with the Builder cult comes to light, and the churches later learn it has been operating outside its dictates for some time.
keys: The Church of Purity and the Lasalle Family
94.name: The Church of Purity and the Lasalle Family

95.content: The church of Undeath serves the god of undeath and raises the unliving. It is stamped out wherever it is found, lies dormant for generations, and strikes only when given a chance. Its priests are unliving things led by Garth Larosse. A past plague: a zombie plague had "a Temple of Undeath at the heart of it all", with the local mayor as high priest.
95.name: The Church of Undeath

96.content: The church of the Healer is the institution through which most healing on Pallimustus is done, with its priests drawing their abilities from the god's essences and awakening stones. It is strongest in isolated areas, and its Greenstone branch is the subject of the first great church scandal in the books.
96.name: The Church of the Healer

97.content: Burning Violet is an old, elite guild based in Vitesse, tied to the Remore family and the Remore Academy. Origin and links: "an old guild, but after Rufus' grandfather became guild leader, it became more and more associated with the Remore Academy". Its membership is Rufus's family plus allies such as Gary and Farrah. Members: most big-family graduates of the Academy do not join, so it is mostly graduates who do not come from power or money. The Academy's scouting programme gives scholarships to people with potential. Symbol: purple flames in the shape of a flower on a belt buckle. Farrah introduces herself as "Burning Violet guild, although I don't have a guild pin on me". Induction: Miles Cotezee says Jason's team has been "inducted into the Burning Violet".
97.name: The Burning Violet Guild

key: Guild Quotas and the Contribution Board
98.comment: Guild Quotas and the Contribution Board
98.content: During a monster surge the Adventure Society assigns every adventurer a minimum action quota, and runs a contribution board as an incentive on top. Guilds are given the bulk of the quotas and compete for the board's non-material rewards. Action quotas: after clearance an adventurer is "assigned an action quota" and must report regularly to the jobs hall for contracts. "Action quotas are the minimum requirements every adventurer has to fulfil during the monster surge". The contribution board: contracts taken beyond the quota carry contribution point values, tallied on weekly and overall leaderboards, with rewards each week and major rewards at the end of the surge. A large leaderboard in the jobs hall shows the top hundred contributors by action quota. Who pays for the rewards: societies, associations and governments give out hefty rewards; in return the Adventure Society "assigns high contribution point values to the contracts that provide that protection". What guilds want: the big guilds monopolise the top of the board, but want "access to civic services" and organisational benefits from the Adventure Society, Magic Society and Alchemy Association, not material rewards. Material rewards are the lower-rung prizes, which small guilds and independents can reach.
keys: Guild Quotas and the Contribution Board
98.name: Guild Quotas and the Contribution Board

99.content: The Sapphire Crown is the royal guild of Rimaros: a guild that works directly for the royal family, whose members rotate through the royal guard. It carries real power, and is held to the same surge quotas as any other guild. Purpose: in many places the role of guard had become ceremonial; "in Rimaros, the solution came in the form of a guild". Royal support: it is one of the most powerful guilds in Rimaros because of the support of the royal family, many of whom are among its most capable members; in return all non-royal members "were required to periodically serve within the royal guard". Membership: stringent, mostly from guild families; loyalty is paramount. All members are examined quarterly, rising to monthly or weekly while serving in the guard. Quotas: the royal family does not shield it from the guilds' activity quotas. Trenchant Moore, a human gold-ranker in a guild of celestines, carries a good portion. Liberty: even its gold-rankers have "a rich amount of liberty", an exception to the usual monitoring of gold-rankers. Standing: Liara is "a figure of accomplishment and respect in the Sapphire Crown", where power, not legacy, is the ultimate authority. Operations: it joins Amouz family members in sweeping the Builder cult's hideouts, watches over a familiar ritual, and uses the duelling arena as a training hall.
99.name: The Sapphire Crown Guild

key: Team Shining Scabbard and the Mirror Kingdom's Backing
100.comment: Team Shining Scabbard and the Mirror Kingdom's Backing
100.content: Team Shining Scabbard is the adventuring team of Prince Valdis of the Mirror Kingdom, built around the healer Sigrid Freyn. The text calls it a royal-backed team, not a guild; the plan's "backers" are the Mirror King's family and the kingdom's resources. This file records what is stated. Origin: Jason says Valdis, "Prince of the Mirror Kingdom", is "the reason their team exists". Humphrey says its members "were being prepared for Valdis's team before any of them ever received an essence". Structure: "their team is built around their healer, Sigrid. She facilitates and directs strategy"; the strategic core is Sigrid and the political core is Valdis. The match: in the mirage chamber fight Jason's team defeats it by going for Sigrid while feinting at Valdis.
keys: Team Shining Scabbard and the Mirror Kingdom's Backing
100.name: Team Shining Scabbard and the Mirror Kingdom's Backing

101.content: House Amouz is a Rimaros noble house that controls or has a share in more than half of the mining operations in the Sea of Storms. Its heir is captured by the Builder cult in Book 8, and the family sends its people in numbers to the cleanup in Book 9. Business: House Amouz "controls or has an interest in more than half of the mining operations in the Sea of Storms, including the bulk of high-rank mineral acquisition". Ties to the royals: Liara's husband married out of House Amouz into the royal family, but remains a high-level manager in the family's business interests. Heir: Gibson Amouz is "son of Lord Cassin Amouz and heir to the seat of House Amouz". He is captured by the cult, which wants the family's secrets. Lord Cassin: a gold-ranker with a goatee, who confronts Liara over his son's capture. Liara suspects the son was targeted because of what he would be told on becoming gold rank and ready to assume his seat. Volunteers: the Amouz family volunteers in numbers that surprise even Liara in the sweep of the hideouts.
101.name: House Amouz

102.content: The Davones are a Greenstone family with close ties to the Mercers who were, in effect, servants of that family for years. Mercer ties: "the Davone and Kettering families, with their close ties to the Mercers" sent their boys to the Mercer compound, where Neil spent time as a boy. Teaming: the Davone and Mercer families "colluded to team him with Thadwick Mercer at a young age".
102.name: House Davone

103.content: The Gellers are an adventuring dynasty with branches across the world and a seat at an estate in the Greenstone delta. They hold only a small provincial title, train their young hard in Greenstone, and are the richest family in the city. The estate: the Geller family estate sits behind a thick high wall, so vast that monsters are as likely to be inside as out; household guards are iron-rank essence users. The seat is "a sprawling estate in the delta", landscaped on secure ground with artful waterways and decades of defences. Standing: "The Geller family stood at the peak of Greenstone society, and their local power was just a fragment of their world-spanning influence". The family "sprawled across continents", and branch families exist: one patriarch leads a branch family. Training: Geller family tradition is to supply scions with enough awakening stones to get started, while the rest must be earned. The family trains its young at "the south end of nowhere" so they can make their own mistakes, with facilities including a mirage chamber and arena. Why Greenstone: other Greenstone families envy the influence the Gellers hold elsewhere and want outside connections. Some families "simply wanted the next adventure", as the Gellers do. The academy annex: the Remore Academy's Greenstone annex is a joint venture with the Gellers, with an internal Geller faction opposed to the agreement.
103.name: House Geller

104.content: The Ketterings are a Greenstone family tied to the Mercers who send their sons to the Mercer compound. They have people in Old City and supply adventurers, including Dustin and Hudson Kettering. Mercer ties: the Davone and Kettering families have "close ties to the Mercers" and send their boys to Thadwick. Adventurers: Hudson Kettering is on Beth Cavendish's team. Dustin Kettering, a local, takes Jonah's defender role in Rick's team. Old City: "The Ketterings have people in Old City"; Danielle coordinates with the Kettering family to mobilise them. Dustin: a friend of Neil's from Thadwick's team. His family obliged him to work with the Mercers.
104.name: House Kettering

105.content: The Mercers are a very powerful Greenstone family, tied to the Duke through marriage, who run spirit coin farms and shape the city's other families through their patronage. Thadwick Mercer is their heir; Cassandra is his sister. Power: "Thadwick's Mercer family was very powerful in Greenstone", and more so when "the Duke of Greenstone's brother, Thadwick's father, married into it". The family ranks above many others, especially those without aristocratic title. Residence: their main residence is a manor on the Island, five towers set in a ring connected by glass walkways, "a feat of magical engineering". Numbers: no family can match the Gellers' numbers, but the Mercers "still made an impressive showing". Farms: Humphrey says most of the spirit coin farms are operated by his family or the Mercers, under Magic Society regulation. The Mercers do not offer part ownership as the Gellers do. Household: the household staff are "raked over the coals" when Thadwick is provoked. Patronage: "Thadwick had needed friends his own age and the Davone and Kettering families, with their close ties to the Mercers, had frequently sent their own boys over". Neil Davone grew up at the Mercer compound.
105.name: House Mercer

key: House Remore and the Remore Academy
106.comment: House Remore and the Remore Academy
106.content: The Remores are a family of educators and adventurers in Vitesse who hold no title but run the Remore Academy, one of the most respected adventurer schools in the world. Roland Remore, a diamond-ranker, is arch-chancellor; Rufus is the heir. The Academy: the family "operates the Remore Academy, which is a big deal everywhere, not just Vitesse". It runs a Greenstone training annex built with the Gellers. Roland: "Although Roland Remore was rarely spotted on the Remore Academy campus, the presence of the diamond-rank arch-chancellor was always felt". Rufus as heir: Rufus "was the prince of Remore Academy, the talented heir-apparent to the power and prestige of his family legacy". Graduates: an academy graduate should have better control of her aura, so students have standing among adventurers. No title: the Remore family has no aristocratic title; the family's prestige comes from "generations of accomplishment", not their name. Like other prestige families they are offered titles and refuse. Scholarships: Rufus's grandfather set up a scouting programme for people with potential, with scholarships and dormitories. Students: scions of international mercantile guilds, adventuring families, aristocrats and royalty, taught by methodology studied from across the globe. The family nurtured Rufus's talent with carefully engineered opportunities. Guild influence: some in the Burning Violet guild think the Academy has too much influence over guild affairs.
keys: House Remore and the Remore Academy
106.name: House Remore and the Remore Academy

key: House Rimaros (the Royal House of Rimaros)
107.comment: House Rimaros (the Royal House of Rimaros)
107.content: The royal family of Rimaros rules the sky-island city and its kingdom under a Storm King. It has its own guild (the Sapphire Crown), marries into the engineering and mining houses for stability, and carries sapphire hair and eyes. The guild: the royal family supports the Sapphire Crown, and many of its own are among its most capable members. See Sapphire_Crown.md. Marriage politics: Zara, a princess, is matched with a member of House Irios, the pre-eminent producer of defensive engineering. The union would have created political stability before the surge. Liara's husband was born into House Amouz. Family traits: Zareen has "the iconic sapphire hair and eyes". Liara: a gold-rank member of the royal house, in charge of screening adventurers for Builder cultists. Zara: although she left the royal family for political reasons, "the Storm King did not stop caring for his daughter".
keys: House Rimaros (the Royal House of Rimaros)
107.name: House Rimaros (the Royal House of Rimaros)

108.content: Greenstone is a colony city at the mouth of a river delta in the low-magic far south of the Africa-like continent. It is the first city Jason knows on Pallimustus and the setting of most of Books 1-3. It was founded because its conditions suit low-end spirit coin farms: stable low magic, in a place that is also livable and close to the desert. It is a place of green marble, walled harbours, crime lords with gentlemanly manners, and a Society full of ambitious, mid-ranked people who use monster cores rather than fight for their ranks. Colonial status: the city began as a colony from the wider kingdom. The Adventure Society is a major force, but the isolation makes the local branch dependent on local powers; Rufus's remark to the village mayor is that "compromises must be made."; The Adventure Society branch is directed by Elspeth Arella. Vincent Trenslow runs assessments and assigns contracts. The Magic Society branch is directed by Lucian Lamprey, a silver-ranker who watches Fortress fights from a viewing box. His deputy is Pochard Finn, whose son Cassowary serves as Lucian's dogsbody. The Big Three of the underworld: Clarissa Ventress (mansion in the canal district), Cole Silva (obsessed with Sophie) and Adris Dorgan. They keep the underworld running and avoid gang war because it draws the attention of the Island authorities.
108.name: Greenstone

109.content: The Storm Kingdom is a nation of islands in the Sea of Storms, founded by Soramir Rimaros, a diamond-ranker who was its first king. Its principal city, Rimaros, spans three islands and is protected by storm accumulators. Its monarch, the Storm King, must be gold-rank; the successor is chosen by the previous king after a contest. Its royal guard is supplied by the Sapphire Crown guild, whose members are examined quarterly, and more often in the guard. It is the first place Jason lands when he returns to Pallimustus in Book 7, just as a monster surge begins. The Sapphire Crown: the royal guild; non-royals serve in the royal guard and take quarterly exams. Commander of the royal guard: Trenchant Moore, introduced as "Commander Trenchant Moore of the royal guard" and called "the siege sword". House Irios: "the pre-eminent producer of defensive engineering" whose defences protect Rimaros and many fortress towns; the family is "known as the shield of" the kingdom. The text of its founder being Soramir's "brother" is not checked here. The Magic Society holds the second-largest sky island in Rimaros, after the palace. The Adventure Society in Rimaros registers Jason and Farrah and questions the irregularities in his record. Politics: Jason's relationship with the throne is called the Storm Kingdom's most important political relationship by Soramir and Zila. Founded by Soramir Rimaros.
109.name: Rimaros (the Storm Kingdom)

110.content: Vitesse, in the kingdom of Estercost, is the City of Flowers, "located in what Jason Asano would know as the French Riviera". Its skyline is made of the garden towers: huge towers with flowering vines spilling down the exterior, "most had every third or fourth floor dedicated to gardens using water, light and plant magic", which are residences for the wealthy elite and headquarters of key organisations. It is a high-magic, wealthy city (the social programmes and labour laws described below are not confirmed in the lines read). It is the home of Remore Academy and of Burning Violet, and the place Rufus, Gary and Farrah come from. Governed within the kingdom of Estercost. The books disagree on where the Adventure Society's continental council sits: Book 6 says "the continental council for the Adventure Society sat in Vitesse, rather than the capital city, Cyrion", while Book 7 calls Cyrion "home to the Adventure Society's continental council". Remore family influence is pervasive: Roland Remore, a diamond-ranker who took over Burning Violet long ago, is the Academy's arch-chancellor and Rufus's grandfather. Burning Violet is the Remore family's elite guild. Strong labour protections and social programmes mean an unusually large comfortable middle class.
110.name: Vitesse

111.content: Yaresh is a rainforest city with "only a few tens of thousands" of people, spread over "the footprint of a much larger centre" because its design deeply accommodates the natural environment. Its walls are "a line of massive trees with walls of glossy black stone filling the gaps", with tunnels through the trunks. It is the centre of the Battle of Yaresh in Book 9 and the gateway to the natural array beneath it. Ruled by a duke, who attends the arena and sends representatives with Adventure and Magic Society convoys. The Aristocratic Faction, a bloc of wealthy aristocrats and merchant barons who own most of the land and provide most of the jobs, is the dominant political force in the region; see 05_Organisations/Guilds_and_Houses.md. Two diamond-rank adventurers live here: Allayeth and Charist, both elves. Hana Shavar is "the High Priestess of the Church of the Healer for the city of Yaresh"; she runs relief for refugees, and after the messenger attack much of Yaresh's population is homeless and housed at Jason's cloud palace. Adventure Society presence is strong; Rufus stays in Yaresh during part of Book 9. Before the series: the natural array and the Smoulder city of Cardinas lie beneath Yaresh. Book 8: Jason's team learns of Yaresh while dealing with Builder and messenger activity.
111.name: Yaresh

112.content: An ancient, circular, overgrown city in an astral space with a sea around it, entered through the drowned fortress at Sky Scar Lake. It is the site of Emir Bahadir's contest for the Scythe of the Reaper, a trial gauntlet that tests wisdom, courage, capability, intellect and resolve.
112.name: The City of Fallen Echoes (Book 2)

113.content: A water-and-islands astral space reached from the desert by a submerged aperture. A large Greenstone expedition goes in at the climax of Book 1 to find what is disrupting it. They are ambushed by a construct army.
113.name: The Desert Astral Space (Book 1)

114.content: An artificial astral space that turns out to be a giant Builder boarding vessel. The Order of the Reaper repurposed its delivery system into a portal system powered by Jason-like power. The team enters it around the middle of Book 3.
114.name: The Reaper-Trials Boarding Vessel (Book 3)

key: Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom
115.comment: Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom
115.content: Jason's personal space grows over the series: a dimensional inventory that only he can physically enter becomes the Spirit Vault, which those who trust him completely can enter, then a spirit domain, a soul realm that travels along the world link, and finally an astral kingdom once he possesses an astral throne and gate. Places inside it are described below.
keys: Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom
115.name: Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom

116.content: A transformation zone is a sealed dome or sphere in which a place is rewritten; the Kostroma sphere extends underground and completely encapsulates the city. Inside is a genesis space: a landscape of anomalies, territories and cores. In Book 5 Dawn names the danger "dimensional ulceration" and says the worst case is that the dimensional membrane rapidly collapses and the world is annihilated, tearing a chunk out of reality; it is more likely contained to the planet or at least the solar system. She adds that "in the best case it will establish a second source of magic that will start feeding into this world".
116.name: Transformation Zones and Genesis Space

117.content: Casselton Beach is Jason's hometown, a tourist beach town on the Mid-North Coast of New South Wales where he was born. It is where he wakes in Book 4 after dying on Pallimustus, and it is the model for the head-shaped fortress he later builds in a transformation zone. Asano Village is the family compound on clifftop land nearby, built by the family after the magic arrives. Book 4: Jason wakes in the hospital; contacts uncle Hiro through the Stone Wall bar in Sydney's Kings Cross; reveals magic to his niece Emi, then to the family. Books 5-6: the family evacuates to Asano Village when the Grid is sabotaged.
117.name: Casselton and Asano Village

key: Incursion Sites (Dorrigo, Makassar, Broken Hill and others)
118.comment: Incursion Sites (Dorrigo, Makassar, Broken Hill and others)
118.content: An incursion is a proto-astral space that opens on Earth and spills monsters into the surrounding area. Spaces are rated by category and last "forty-three hours, as a baseline". This file records the sites where the story takes place.
keys: Incursion Sites (Dorrigo, Makassar, Broken Hill and others)
118.name: Incursion Sites (Dorrigo, Makassar, Broken Hill and others)

119.content: Nitra, in western Slovakia, is a city that became "a major centre for the Network after the organization had been pushed out of Bratislava by vampires". It is too small to host ancient vampires but large enough to warrant Network protection. At the end of Book 5 a transformation zone forms there; in Book 6 Jason claims it and it becomes his first Earth spirit domain.
119.name: Nitra (Slovakia)

120.content: Saint-Étienne, France, is the site of the Dimensional Fortress, a permanent astral space found by the Network's Lyon branch in 1948. In Book 4 Jason frees Farrah from it; in Book 6 it becomes a second transformation zone, which Jason claims and later turns into a whimsical cloud city of refugees.
120.name: Saint-Étienne (France)

121.content: Arcazitlan is a fortress town dug into the wall of a rocky gorge in jungle country, where Jason arrives alone at the start of the surge and fights bone feasters. Its region is not named in the lines checked. Book 7: Jason lands nearby after dropping from the sky, reaches the fort during a night attack by bone feasters (emaciated, eyeless humanoid monsters with large mouths) and helps defend it; he leaves by road with Shade as a land skimmer.
121.name: Arcazitlan

122.content: Boko is an old desert city of academics and artists to the north of Greenstone, with a native population, a Duke, an Adventure Society branch and a Magic Society presence. Jason first arrives there by portal at the end of the Ustei expedition. The scholars: "Scholars of the arts. Painting, poetry, sculpture, dance"; people travel from across the continent to visit its theatres. People: almost entirely human and very dark-skinned, with local fashion loose and breathable, calmer than the Ustei's. Rule: a Duke of Boko, a silver-ranker through cores, as is normal for political leaders; noble houses exist. Adventurers: the Adventure Society has a branch, but Boko "was not a strong adventuring city". Trouble: a movement against intellectuals among low-rankers began in Boko proper before it spread out; officials suspect more sinister backing and a power base shift to Greenstone and Boko. Book 1: the Adventure Society returns the Ustei captives to Boko, where Jason arrives through Hester's portal; he, Gary and Rufus explore it. After the assassination the city is evacuated, the blast containment zone gives out and the city is gone; most of its ninety thousand people are evacuated. They shelter in Jason's astral kingdom.
122.name: Boko

123.content: Cartise was a river city and the major hub of trade and travel in its area, destroyed just before the great surge when the Builder cult claimed a nearby astral space and a diamond-rank monster then overwhelmed the city. Jason's team clears monsters from its ruins in Book 9. Before: "the river city of Cartise", the major hub for trade and travel in the area. It had many adventurers who now protect the fortress towns. The fall: the Builder cult claimed a nearby astral space, which separated from the world with widespread destruction; a diamond-rank monster manifested shortly after and overwhelmed the city; most people were evacuated to towns along the river. After: the ruins look like London after the Blitz, with blocks reduced to fist-sized rubble. Refugees overpopulate the surrounding towns and the loss strains logistics. Clearing the ruins: Jason's team sweeps a route guided by an Adventure Society functionary named Vestine, as one of several teams.
123.name: Cartise

124.content: Casallini is a small border city of Girlano, close to the coast where Girlano comes nearest to the Sea of Storms. It is where Sophie's Book 8 delivery contract leads, and where a gang is hired to ambush her on behalf of Purity loyalists. Gangs and cartels: the surrounding country is run by cartels producing heavily controlled or banned substances from rare plants and minerals. The eight men who ambush Sophie are members of a small gang from the nearby city, one of many satellite groups to the local cartel, mostly strongmen who keep low-end officials in line. Hired muscle: they are silver-rank in their forties, "raw garbage" with no training and reeking of cores, hired by Purity loyalists to bring Sophie in. Adventure Society presence: the Society ignores borders and keeps monsters out of population centres; its neutrality is why Sophie heads this way, and Liara says "we have a large force in Casallini because it's a border city". Smuggler's paths: semi-hidden paths through jungle-covered hills avoid border checkpoints, which have no patrols during the surge. Character: "a lawless town full of crappy guys" in Sophie's words.
124.name: Casallini

125.content: Girlano is a landlocked inland nation south of the Storm Kingdom, ostensibly a kingdom but controlled by cartels that produce heavily controlled or banned substances, with a puppet government. It is a smuggling region on the Storm Kingdom's border. Cartels: the illicit leadership keeps its position through under-the-table deals with powerful groups in neighbouring countries, which prop up the puppet government while their own governments pay lip service to suppression. Trade: the rare plants and minerals of the region are what the cartels exploit, and strong public sanctions and border controls surround the nation. Adventure Society: it ignores borders and politics and keeps monsters out of population centres, so long as its work is not interfered with. Reputation: Liara calls it "a stain full of drug dealers and smugglers"; Belinda finds it "famously sketchy" and tempting. Book 8: Sophie heads toward Girlano and Casallini on a specialised delivery. Book 9: the team turns east at the coast, not south toward Girlano.
125.name: Girlano

126.content: Hornis is a port city on the coast south and around from Greenstone, reached overland through the delta, the veldt and then south. It is Greenstone's nearest rival port, used for smuggling and escapes, and a stop on the team's route home in Book 9. Adventure Society: Hornis has a branch that mounts large searches. Magic Society: Hornis has its own Magic Society people and a mirage chamber that Danielle helped rebuild and maintains. Underworld: the Big Three's influence is a factor in Greenstone; Sophie plans to buy her way past it in Hornis. Book 1: Sophie plans to flee through the delta and the veldt to Hornis with the spirit coin vault's money. Book 2: smuggled materials are traced to shipments into Hornis before being moved to private vessels; Jonah's team is found in Hornis on a boat bound for distant shores. Book 3: Lucian Lamprey hopes to escape to Hornis through a contact. Book 9: the team's route home runs south, across the Great Southern Continent, then north to Hornis on the way to Greenstone, Vitesse and Cyrion.
126.name: Hornis

127.content: Isart is named once: a city on Jason's procession south where Emir asks to meet him to discuss a job and bring the person who made the cloud flasks. Emir says there is "a city called Isart that you should arrive at on your procession south", will meet Jason there when the detour is done, will arrive in about two weeks and bring the maker of the cloud flasks. No later scene in the chapter files shows Jason reaching Isart, and nothing describes the city.
127.name: Isart

128.content: Jayapura is a port on the northern coast of Pranay, the large southern land equivalent to Sri Lanka, and the birthplace of Hester. Jason's team stays several days after the Reaper trial to awaken abilities, summon familiars and get tattoos. Mirage Chamber Association: owns the complex, has close ties to the Magic Society, Adventure Society and local government and holds significant power. Entertainment: essence users fight one another or illusions for a paying audience.
128.name: Jayapura

129.content: Kurdansk is a river city in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil and Sophie Wexler's birthplace. It has a busy skyport, an entertainment quarter in a former warehouse district, many dark-skinned, silver-haired celestines and prisons that hold criminals for years. For the culture see../../04_Peoples_and_Cultures/Kurdansk_Culture.md. Peoples: celestines with dark skin and silver hair are common. Book 6: Emir tells Sophie she was born in Kurdansk; the team searches the city, and Marta Fries, a silver-rank celestine and friend of Melody Jain, escapes through a hidden panel Melody once used to fake her death, about two decades earlier. Book 9: Melody Jain's story begins in Kurdansk about twenty-five years before; she and Sophie's father were both secret members of organisations, the Order of the Reaper among them.
129.name: Kurdansk

130.content: Leust is one of the largest and richest towns in the delta, with paved roads and stone buildings instead of mud brick. Jason stays there while investigating a fergax contract in the nearby lumber region. Industry: lumber; the land rights are heavily regulated, and the lumber region is one of the few places in the delta where lumber-worthy trees grow. Mill owners: Kyle Lindover, a leonid larger than Gary, owns the Lindover Lumber Mill and shut it after repeated fergax sightings; his family stays with her parents in Greenstone.
130.name: Leust

131.content: Two neighbouring lumber properties in the eastern delta, near Leust: Kyle Lindover's idle mill and the busy, ostentatious property of Eustace Clementson. In Book 1 a "fergax" sighting contract Jason takes turns out to be a land-grab staged by Thadwick Mercer, and the properties are where he finds the summoner behind it.
131.name: The Lindover and Clementson Properties

132.content: Oleyu is an unremarkable border city on a river, "pleasant, prosperous, and moderately sized", built on river trade with a mid-range level of magic. Position: Clive's route follows a river to "the border city of Oleyu", where the Rakesh Magic Society branch's area of influence ends. Standing: not as big or important as Rakesh or Vitesse, or unusual like Greenstone. Magic Society building: Clive lodges a protest here over his treatment by the Rakesh branch, without optimism.
132.name: Oleyu

133.content: Palisaros is a small laid-back town on the island of Arnote in the Storm Kingdom, arranged along a lagoon and the clifftop above it, where Jason settles his cloud house. Residents: mostly normals, irons and bronzes using cores, with a few silver and gold auras, and many caramel-skinned celestines. Pace: small-town, with none of the residents in a rush, calmer than busy Livaros. Mayor: Pelli, a member of the royal family but separate from them, living a relatively humble life as a core user. Guide: Argy shows visitors the saloon, eateries and market. Book 7: Jason meets Argy and Pelli in the town and settles there; during the surge only Jason and Pelli remain to defend it, and Jason leaves shortly after his team. Book 8: Vidal rides into the lagoon to find Wexler's team staying in a house by the waterfall.
133.name: Palisaros

134.content: Rakesh is a populous, caste-divided city on the north coast of the Africa-like continent, home of the Adventure Society's continental council and of the continent's largest Magic Society and Adventure Society strongholds. It is where the Magic Society holds Clive in all but name and where Danielle meets Carlivexistrix. Caste system: society is divided into castes, and the caste system justifies holding someone seen as lowly against their will; it dismisses Belinda as unimportant. Culture: busy but quiet streets, a local culture that values calm decorum, most people on foot or in animal-drawn carriages. The Magic Society branch: one of the most powerful on the continent; officials there have power and connections, so consequences come from the Adventure Society, not other branches. The campus prevents portals outside designated zones. The Adventure Society: the continental council sits here. Vitesse is also described as the seat of a continental council; the text reads most simply as one council per continent, with Rakesh serving the Africa-like continent and Vitesse the continent of Estercost, but it never states this.
134.name: Rakesh

135.content: Zartos is a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines, and the home of the diamond-rank smith Virid, Gary's mentor. It is named early as a celestine centre and appears on the page only when Gary and Virid reforge Jason's sword there. Peoples: "Zartos has a large celestine community"; the city is "largely populated by celestines". No ruler or institution is named in the lines checked. Book 1: Gary and Farrah mention Zartos on the road; Rufus has not been there, though his brother recommended it. Book 7: after Jason's death the team waits in Zartos while Gary and Virid examine and reforge Dread Salvation, a collaboration that Jason's soul-bond guides; the sword returns as Hegemon's Will.
135.name: Zartos

136.content: The continent that Jason would call Africa holds Greenstone, where Books 1-3 are set. In the text it is separate from Eurasia (see the World Primer), is far more populous in the north than the south, and has its continental Adventure Society and Magic Society strongholds at Rakesh on the north coast. This file sets out the places the compendium already files here, from south to north.
136.name: The Africa-like Continent

137.content: Estercost is the kingdom whose capital Cyrion is the largest city in the world and whose Vitesse sits on the equivalent of the French Riviera. The text places it on the Europe-like continent and calls it the home of Greenstone's founders. It is the setting of most of Books 6 and 11 and the base of Remore Academy and the Burning Violet guild.
137.name: Estercost and Its Continent

138.content: The Storm Kingdom is a nation of islands in the Sea of Storms, the Caribbean analogue, founded by Soramir Rimaros. Its best-known city, Rimaros, spans three public islands; its largest and most populous city is Jaitari. Beyond the islands lies Girlano, the cartel country along its southern border.
138.name: The Storm Kingdom's Islands

139.content: The Network's Lyon Operations Director, who imprisons Farrah in the dimensional fortress, rises to be the second "Mr East" and later follows Gerling. Operations Director of the Network's Lyon branch, working out of the black site; one of the secretive staff who knew of and worked in the dimensional fortress, and has been cultivating loyalists. He leaves the dimensional space by another aperture just before it is sealed, alone, with no EOA and no prisoner. In Book 5 he takes the seat of Mr East, speaking of "the previous Mr East" and of vetting his people. Mr North says his own minions were disappointing before Barbou came along. Anna says Barbou is not hers to give; Farrah says "Barbou belongs to me". Gerling hits him and demands help reaching the Saint-Étienne dimensional space. In the zone he is the only one not attacked by the soul attacks and Jason declines to take him. In 2038 Farrah recalls him as the man behind her incarceration and tells Anna to retire the "bad apple" excuse. Jason brought him out of the zone alive; Mr North asked for a quick death and Jason left the decision to Farrah, who describes disposing of bodies without denying what she did, so Anna concludes "Barbou isn't alive". In Book 6 Anna did not know his fate.
139.name: Adrien Barbou

140.content: A gold-rank adventurer with a soul-damaged aura who teaches Jason aura and soul techniques and is lost to an orb in Cardinas. Trenchant asks whether anyone has worked with Amos Pensinata. Dawn names him as a gold-ranker whose experiences with soul trauma left him with a more capable aura than most; she has convinced him to travel with Jason to teach soul manipulation. Jason knows him by reputation as the man who defeated the same forces that had forced Jason to flee the underwater complex. Jason later learns from him how to combine auras into a single force and about controlling aspects of the soul in isolation, which helped him expand perception without a beacon-like aura. Clive turns on him at the Yaresh camp: "You were brought on to help Jason, not make things worse. But your baggage...". He debriefs a Rimaros team in Cardinas and is among the few able to resist the zone's corruption. His nephew is Orin Pensinata; he joins Jason's journey partly because Orin insisted on coming. Jason extracts him from his attempted "suicide-by-messenger" and the gold-rankers escape into Jason's soul realm. After the zone he takes Orin and the scout Rosa back to Rimaros.
140.name: Amos Pensinata

141.content: Anisa Lasalle is a zealous elf priestess of Purity from the Lasalle family who guides Rufus's party in Book 1, is thrown out for killing a captive, and dies serving the Builder's cult alliance in Book 3. Cold, righteous and quick to anger, she treats mercy as weakness. Zealous: Rufus calls her "Zealous girl. Dangerously committed". Ruthless: Farrah says "Anisa killed him before he could get a word out". Defiant of correction: Gary tells her "You don't get a say in what we do anymore, Anisa... You're out". In the Book 3 fight she is "something of a perfect weapon against Jason's powers", able to protect herself and cleanse afflictions. A temporary addition to Rufus's party at the start of the books. After Purity is implicated in the cult she vanishes with the archbishop and much of the Lasalle family. Rufus and Farrah: former party leaders. Nicolas Hendren: her archbishop.
141.name: Anisa Lasalle

142.content: She is Jason's most trusted political contact on Earth. Family: wife Susan; brother Terrance, the Network's media director. Habits: Nigel Thornton's team is most often contracted by her, and Nigel says he came to Rexion on her job.
142.name: Annabeth "Anna" Tilden

143.content: Argy (Emmett Dillivan) is a fruit grower in Palisaros who takes Jason, Rufus and Farrah into town and to the mayor, Pelli. Easygoing and proud of his town, he treats visitors as guests. Laconic: Jason "happily fell into Argy's laconic pace". Hospitable: he greets everyone he passes in the sealed streets. Friendly nickname: "Emmett Dillivan, but folks just call me Argy". Not an essence user in the lines read; his family has grown the fruit "longer than most can remember". Named for the fruit he is eating, which looks like a large tangerine. Pelli: local mayor; he says "You'll want to talk to Pelli". Jason: calls Palisaros "a genuine paradise".
143.name: Argy

144.content: Asya Karadeniz is a school friend of Jason's from the Mid North Coast who works in Network magitech administration. She joins Jason's side in Book 4, crews Kaito's helicopter with Greg, enters Jason's spirit vault as their relationship deepens, and dies in the Berlin attack in Book 5. Her family stays in the Asano clan afterwards. Dry about herself: "I was always fancy". Modest about her job: "I'm just an administrator there... My job is to keep the people doing the actual work happy and funded". Deliberate in contact: she asked for the Sydney slot because she went to school with Jason. Shaken by the gap between boy and man: the recording of Jason's power unnerved her, set against "the boy she had known" with his "sexy, impish grin". An executive-level Network administrator given an essence to reach category one, without monster cores. She operates the helicopter's weapons when a winged lizard enters her sights. Went to school with Jason and Greg. Her mother Rabia sits on the Asano Village committee for the non-Asano families and helps introduce the village to magic. Her cousin is Lina Karadeniz, who is also Emi's friend. Jason: old school friend; she enters his spirit vault "as her relationship with Jason deepened". Greg and Kaito: teammates. Anna: "The bastards killed Asya". Rabia and the Karadeniz family: mother and relatives.
144.name: Asya Karadeniz

145.content: Liara Rimaros's husband and their three silver-rank children. Baseph is Liara's husband, silver rank, met leaving her townhouse. In Book 8 he hammers a pipe to draw raiders, fears what lies below because it is people who died because of what he did and is saved by Jason. He holds Liara's hand under the table. Dara is the eldest, a one-star adventurer happy to hunt monsters, with Liara's height and Baseph's dark copper hair and eyes, a muscular frontline combatant. Zareen is the middle child, physically smaller, with the royal family's sapphire hair and eyes, a politics enthusiast close to Vesper and a three-star adventurer. Joseph is the youngest and only son, an administrative official with the Amouz family business interests like his father; he wants to meet the man who saved his father. Dara's later remark about "the one from up north" with the elf twins refers to Rick.
145.name: Baseph, Dara, Zareen and Joseph

146.content: Belinda "Lindy" Callahan is Sophie's oldest friend, a thief from Greenstone's Old City who becomes Clive's assistant and, in time, the team's planner, infiltrator and master of shapeshifting. Essences: Magic, Trap and Adept, which she traded for in Book 2, producing the Charlatan confluence. Abilities: Echo Spirit is her first charlatan ability; Bait and Switch, Rune Trap, Force Tether, Lightning Tether and Pit of the Reaper; shapeshifting. Storage: a personal storage space that even the Magic Society cannot peek into "without killing her first". Familiars: Shimmer, a summoned astral lantern, and an echo spirit that looks like a blurry version of her.
146.name: Belinda Callahan

147.content: Benella is a servant of the messengers who works as Zolit's aide, brings Jason to the messengers' attention and is given one chance to prove herself valuable. Careful, watchful and afraid, she hides what she thinks behind a servant's neutrality. Neutral by necessity: she is relieved but not fool enough to thank the messenger, as showing that his consideration mattered would get her punished. Self-possessed: "Benella," she corrected with an annoyed shake of her head. Uncertain under scrutiny: she is unsure why Kaal is interested in her thought process. Not an essence user in the lines read; she is Zolit's aide, silent until the priest leaves. Her master is Fal Vin Garath; he scolds her and demands she explain the servant races' different way. Fal Vin Garath: her abusive master. Jes Fin Kaal: the Voice she presents to. Zolit: the fighter she aids.
147.name: Benella

148.content: Beth Cavendish is a bronze-rank Greenstone adventurer and water healer who leads a team in the Ustei campaign and the City of Fallen Echoes. Competent and brisk, she gives orders without ceremony. Brisk: "We're going to move on the sand barge". Encouraging: "Welcome to the path to bronze rank". Compared with Cassandra's brother: Cassandra says the way Jason describes his brother reminds her of Beth. Water healer; Jason envies her affliction-blanketing powers. Struck down by the thorn fountain's retributive damage in the Fallen Echoes fight. Introduces herself to Jason at the Adventure Society as Beth Cavendish, meeting her cousin Mose. The Cavendish family names a Greenstone district. Hudson, Niko, Emily, Mose: team members.
148.name: Beth Cavendish

149.content: A gold-rank stealth assassin, former teammate of Emir and of Rufus's parents, whose long hunt for Sophie's mother Melody Jain drives his later scenes. Introduced by Emir as a gold-ranker who, if he does not want to be seen, cannot be seen by anyone short of diamond rank. Described as "the gold-ranked assassination specialist" and the group's best scout; his attacks on a gold-rank priest land strongly but do not kill at once. He, Gabriel and Arabelle Remore have been companions for decades. Emir, Arabelle, Gabriel and Callum were an old team. An avid monster-hunter, he is one of the few gold-rankers who obsessively raise their strength. He stops Sophie and Humphrey from running off after the Order of the Reaper: "I'm stopping you until you are ready. Hate me if you like", and explains the order split from the cult and became self-serving assassins. His fixation on Melody Jain, Sophie's mother, is because he is connected to her: she kept him as her only real connection to the order; he lost track of her and has searched ever since. Jason avoids his petitions to see Melody, and finds his aura dangerously unstable even after things are in the open.
149.name: Callum Morse

150.content: Cheryl Asano is Jason's mother, from a large Australian farming and mining family. She is the one in the family fascinated with Japan, a strong-willed realtor who shows up in Book 4 stunned at her dead son's return. Strong-willed: she flashes "a well-recognised look of dissatisfaction" at Jason's poke but calms herself. Stern: Jason jokes "Mum is quite stern". Grieving: she looks at Jason "like she'd seen a ghost" and hugs him tightly once she steels her nerve. Overworked: she hasn't been into the office in two days, unlike her. She is "the pre-eminent upscale realtor in the Greater Casselton area". She is non-essence in the lines read; portal travel sickens her. Her family are "miners and farmers, tracing their bloodline back through bushrangers, convicts, and indigenous Australians"; she was the one fascinated with Japan. Her brother is Robert; her mother makes a miraculous recovery. Jason is told his parents divorced a year ago and that his mother moved to Castle Reach. Erika and Kaito: other children. Amy: puts a restraining hand on Cheryl's arm.
150.name: Cheryl Asano

151.content: Clarissa Ventress is one of the crime lords of Old City and holds Sophie's indenture. She uses Sophie to provoke the rash Cole Silva and learns what Lucian Lamprey wants in order to control him. Calculating: "The key to controlling a person was finding what they wanted". Amused: she is "happily imagining the look on Silva's face" as she watches Sophie's match. Irritated by independence: she is less happy with Sophie's friend Belinda. Rank is not stated in the lines read; she travels with a huge leonid bodyguard. Lives in a sprawling manor in Old City's canal district, which has its own internal city wall. Her arrangement with Sophie: Sophie would help her provoke Silva into the kind of rash action his father would have prevented. Sophie: indentured servant. Cole Silva: rival, newest of the Big Three. Lucian Lamprey: someone she plans to control.
151.name: Clarissa Ventress

152.content: Clive Standish is a tall, lanky Magic Society researcher in Greenstone, raised on an eel farm, who becomes Jason's team's ritualist and astral-magic scholar. He explains the cosmos to Jason as a bowl of dumpling soup, identifies the Reaper-trial astral space as a Builder vessel, and builds the open-access Magical Research Association. A lecturer who loses the thread and apologises; he wants dumpling soup in the middle of his own lecture on the cosmos. He says he venerates, not worships, the Celestial Book: "There's a difference"; an archbishop asks "You admit to being a heretic?" and Clive answers that he "could be considered a heretic". He jokes about his background: "I'm the son of eel farmers". A stranger accuses him of sleeping with a wife he says he does not have, which becomes a running gag. Essences: Magic, Rune, Balance and the Karmic confluence. A rune essence came to him as "an epic four-star essence". Abilities: Wrath of the Magister, a rune circle that triggers effects when attacked, the damage-reflecting buff Mantle of Retribution and the zone ability Eye of Karma; Mana Equilibrium. Racial gift: a blessing from the Celestial Book changed his human Special Attack Affinity into a spell affinity. Familiar: Onslow, a rune tortoise who sits at the prow of the airboat, carries Clive, and becomes a runic tattoo on his torso when called back. Ritual and astral magic: he leads the team's rituals and bridge research.
152.name: Clive Standish

153.content: Cole Silva is the newest of Old City's Big Three crime lords, who inherits his father's operation and, with Lucian Lamprey, orchestrates Jason's kidnapping and star seed implantation. Arrested in Book 3, his organisation falls into chaos. Rash: Clarissa plans to provoke him "into the kind of rash action that his father always kept him from making". Predatory: his father's protection of Sophie is gone and he watches her match from a viewing box. His father had a small operation catering to nobles with low tastes, with the money and connections to arrange expensive cleansings. The father died in his sleep "a couple of months ago"; the son stepped up. Cole's father killed a man who tried to rob him. Clarissa Ventress: rival crime lord. Lucian Lamprey: partner in the kidnapping.
153.name: Cole Silva

154.content: Cressida Vane is the matriarch of the blood-cult family that holds Jason and his friends in Book 1. Beautiful, haughty and weary of her family's ambitions, she insists they are "a nice, traditional blood cult family" and she is killed in the confrontation. Haughty: "I am Lady Cressida Vane"; Jason mocks her high-priestess name. Traditional: "This is my manor, my family, and we do things the traditional way". Dismissive of her husband: "I don't care what my stupid husband thinks; he married into the family". Leader of the blood cult family's rituals. Complained that astral beings were "the death" of her son. Mother of Landemere Vane; she asks what Landemere was trying to summon. Darryl: the high priest beside her.
154.name: Cressida Vane

155.content: Danielle Geller is Humphrey's mother and the head of the Geller family's household in Greenstone. She is a silver-ranker at the start of the series who looks much younger than she is, later a gold-ranker with dimension and time powers, and Jason's political adviser on Earth. Time: a time confluence, with only forward time travel possible; in Book 3 she outpaces Lucian Lamprey in a fight, teleporting behind him and cutting his neck. She is called "Time Witch of Vitesse". Dimension: a dimension essence, as Emir says, with gold rank from the notes; she teleports behind Lamprey in a fight. Estate and training: the Geller estate's mirage chamber can run at bronze rank only "for limited periods" because Greenstone's magic is low, and at iron rank Danielle offers it to Rufus; a family member from the generation that first settled the region may still be alive. The diamond-rank ancestor in the earlier notes was not found. Rank: silver in Book 1, gold by Book 7.
155.name: Danielle Geller

156.content: Dawn is the World-Phoenix's First Servant, the head of its cult and its primary vessel. She guides Jason through Books 4-8 as a mentor and agent: she paints, takes avatar bodies, reveals the invasion plan, negotiates with the Builder and brings Jason's friends to Rimaros. Role: First Servant of the World-Phoenix, head of its cult and the primary vessel of the great astral being. Diamond-rank vessels of great astral beings can withstand the strain and keep their selves, and former vessels end up as peak existences. One intervention: the Hierophant is allowed to intervene in Pallimustus a single time; in Book 7 she says she will use one full-power intervention, and she destroys a Builder rolling city with a phoenix. Art: the paintings by "Dawn" that Jason buys show two planets with four pillars and "The Invasion of Pallimustus". Home: Interstice, the city-universe at the cosmos's centre.
156.name: Dawn

157.content: An ice-armoured defender from the Kettering family who starts as one of Thadwick Mercer's offsiders, joins Rick's team in Book 2 and later fights beside Neil in Cardinas. One of Thadwick Mercer's two offsiders with Neil: he protects the group with his powers while Neil heals them. The Davone and Kettering families have close ties to the Mercers, which is how the boys came to Thadwick's side. He and Neil are relieved to be free, having been known as Thadwick's flunkeys. A local who fills Jonah Geller's defender role on Rick's team: "a classic defender, not very mobile but very hard to go around or through", clad in armour forged entirely of ice. His cousin Hudson Kettering is his counterpart on Beth Cavendish's team. In Book 7 he is a friend of Neil's from their time on Thadwick's team; by Book 9 he is the only non-local on Rick's team, picked up after Jonah's death.
157.name: Dustin Kettering

158.content: Emi Evans-Asano is Jason's niece, the daughter of Erika and Ian Evans, whom Jason calls "Moppet". She is twelve when he comes home in Book 4 and learns the truth about magic from him. She trains in ritual magic under Farrah, decides at thirteen that she does not want to fight as he does, and takes her essences at about sixteen under Rufus. The System names her as the contact "Emi Evans-Asano" when Jason returns, and he senses her aura with Erika's and Ian's. Her father says she has always been hard to parent: "You thought you were smarter than me by age seven, and by age nine, you were right.". Jason's remark on her at twelve is "twelve going on forty". Erika says Emi took his death hard and that Erika's own conspiracy-theory phase did not help. Her cousins are Hana and Jace, Kaito and Amy's daughters; her great-grandmother Yumi is "Nana Yumi" to her. At twelve she stands up to a group of boys picking on another student at Jason's old school, which Jason watches through Shade. Jason promises Erika he will tell her everything. Emi guesses something is wrong from how her parents are acting, throws herself into his arms when he appears, and her parents nod their agreement to let her go with him. He takes her for a drive, and she asks whether he is "the Starlight Angel". At a coastal lookout he asks "Do you believe in magic, Emi?", the car dissolves into his shadow, and she says "You're him".
158.name: Emi Evans-Asano

159.content: Emir Bahadir is a gold-rank treasure hunter, patron of the Reaper contest and owner of a cloud ship and palace that becomes Jason's team's base. Elegant, ageless and wanderlustful, he has hunted the remnants of the Order of the Reaper for years, uses his wealth and staff for large schemes, and marries his chief of staff, Constance. Likes grand entrances: "I'm hosting a grand event. It requires grandeur". He announces a competition and a grand-prize cloud palace in a speech that throws the crowd into turmoil. Warm and wry: he tells Rufus "Comrades behind her, enemies in front of her and friends beside her" of Farrah's apparent death and sighs "world-weary" when Jason storms off. Cautious in accusation: "Making that kind of accusation against a church is no small matter and even I'm not completely convinced yet". Not used to being the responsible one: that is Constance's job, but he is the older and higher-ranked man. Essences: he has "staff, might, magic and mystic". Cloud ship and palace: a cloud ship the size of an ocean liner that morphs into a palace. His preferred design is a five-towered castle. Staff and speed: he conjures copies of his staff under every construct, smashing the iron and bronze ones and tossing the silvers and catches Danielle before she can lunge. Aura mastery: he can block the senses of others, normally taught only to gold-rankers.
159.name: Emir Bahadir

160.content: Fal Vin Garath is a silver-rank messenger master who is abusive but within the bounds his peers accept. He detests acting at the behest of Jes Fin Kaal and launches a soul attack on Jason in Book 9. Imperious: he scowls at Benella and demands answers in a voice "like a command from the heavens". Resentful of command: he "detested being forced to act at the behest of the Voice of the Will" and sneers at his commander, astral king's Voice and Asano. Silver rank; he launches a soul attack on Jason through his connection to Shade and is surprised when Jason fends it off and retaliates. He seizes Shade and squeezes while Shade drains his mana, until Shade's body is destroyed. Benella's master, "abusive but not outside the bounds of acceptability to his fellow messengers", free to treat the servant races as he pleased so long as it did not impinge on other messengers. Jes Fin Kaal: his commander. Hess Jor Nasala: sits with him at Kaal's meeting.
160.name: Fal Vin Garath

key: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
161.comment: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
161.content: A familiar is a purely magical creature from the deep astral given a body by a summoning. Jason has three, each very different, and Humphrey has one.
keys: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
161.name: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash

162.content: Farrah Hurin (also spelt Huren) is a small, pale, strawberry-blonde ritual magician from Vitesse. She is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, teaches him aura control, perception and meditation, and treats him as an equal. She dies in Book 1, is brought back by the Reaper, and reappears on Earth in Book 4. Essences: Earth, Fire and Potent, which form the Volcano confluence; she explains this herself in Book 1. Abilities: lava cannon, a magma golem, lava streams and fire orbs, obsidian domes, shards and columns, and obsidian armour. Ritual magic: she adjusts circles for ambient magic and builds the infrastructure of Asano Village and the Grid repairs. Aura teaching: perception and memory games, meditation and aura control.
162.name: Farrah Hurin

163.content: Gareth "Gary" Xandier is an enormous leonid smith and warrior from Vitesse. He makes Jason's first sword, Dread Salvation. Summon: a foundry golem, a roughly three-metre black-iron figure with a molten mouth that drips molten metal. Equipment: conjured full-body dark-steel plate armour; the notes add a hammer and shield and the runes. Smithing: he forges Dread Salvation; he reforges it with his mentor Virid Martine as Hegemon's Will. Rank: bronze at the start; "almost silver" by Book 3; silver after using a core. Demigod: Hero's power makes him a demigod, "a vision of physical might, wreathed in divine power".
163.name: Gary (Gareth Xandier) and Gary Sharpton

164.content: Greg is an old school friend of Jason's who joins the Network defectors on Kaito's helicopter crew and is killed in Book 5. His family is taken into Asano Village afterward. He is nerdy, self-deprecating and braver than he believed. Self-deprecating: he was "never much more than an adequate lawyer" and had been pushed out of his father's practice. Enjoys small comforts: he holds a mug of hot chocolate on a chalet balcony. Teased by Asya: "If all your friends are cool, what does that say about you?". Sensitive to portals: he fights portal sickness on Erika's floor. Bronze rank by Book 5; his body "could easily endure the cold". He crews Kaito's helicopter with Asya. School friend of Jason and Asya who roped Jason and Amy into hours-long board games. He says he had lived more in six months of magic than in six years before. Asya: friend and fellow crew member.
164.name: Greg

165.content: Twin elf sisters on Rick Geller's team: Hannah the archer and Claire the healer. The elf twins Hannah and Claire Adeah are the archer and the team healer, with Claire the most important member to protect. Hannah's arrows pin trap weavers to trees; Claire cleanses afflictions and cuts a team mate from a web with her wand. In the Book 1 mock battle against Jason, Claire's body is left floating in the water after she focused her healing on the others, and they swear revenge. Claire resented Jason's tactics in the mock battle the most.
165.name: Hannah and Claire Adeah

166.content: Hester Maharala is Emir's portal user and head of logistics, born in Jayapura in Pranay. Warm, travelled and practical, she gets people where they need to be and keeps Emir's operations running. Warm and practical: Jason compares her portal range to his own shadow portals. Respected: "Hester was one of Emir's most important staff members". Portal user: she traces a circle in the air to open a portal; she can only open portals to places she has visited and the time before her next use depends on range. She portals Clive back to the city. Born in Jayapura, a port city of Pranay. Has a clifftop house with grotto rooms and a swim-access bar. A shopkeeper calls her "Hester Maharala... The lady with the house on the hill".
166.name: Hester Maharala

167.content: Hudson Kettering is the huge earth-essence front-liner of Beth Cavendish's team and cousin of Dustin Kettering. He is a stone-shielding bruiser who meets Jason on the sand barge assault, fights Humphrey in a Geller-versus-Cavendish contest, and joins the Reaper trial expedition. Size: "One of the members of Beth's team was a huge human named Hudson. He looked like Humphrey with twenty percent bonus person, to the point of being almost as large as Gary". First meeting: he tells Jason "You don't seem evil". Team role: Beth puts him "front and centre" in the assault on the sand barge, and a large flat block of sandstone rises under the team to carry them forward like a raft. In the fight: a bronze-rank captain's charge shatters his stone shield and sends him staggering; he ploughs up the ramp "crashing into the people inside and making space for the others". Beth tells him "No slacking". Family: he is cousin to Dustin, "the only one I can think of who could stack up to Jonah" among defenders, and cannot be pried from Beth's team. Dustin sits beside him with their teams around them. Humphrey's offer: Jason brings Humphrey to talk to Hudson about his cousin joining a Geller team; Hudson says a Geller name is good "but so was Mercer", and the family wants real adventurers for Dustin after Thadwick. Memorial: his team attends the memorial because "Her standing strong is the reason my team all got out alive".
167.name: Hudson Kettering

168.content: Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller is the leader of Team Biscuit, a tall, broad-shouldered, handsome young man from a family that has been adventuring for sixteen generations. He begins the series a shy teenager and becomes a steady leader and one of the team's strongest fighters. Formal in a crisis: in Book 3, facing the Builder's forces, he announces "My name is Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller. My family have been adventurers for sixteen generations. We aren't alchemists or weaponsmiths on the side... For hundreds of years we have done one thing, and one thing only: protect our world from people like you". Shy in personal matters: when Jason asks in front of his mother whether he has spoken to Gabrielle, he turns white and shakes his head. Moral voice: in Book 1 he confronts Jason about the cruelty of the mirage-arena ambush. He later advises against elaborate plans: "We tried that fifteen years ago and we only got from Rimaros to Yaresh". Essences: the dragon confluence, reached through the might and wing essences. Abilities include dragon wings and a flaming dragon-wing sword, a Dragon's Might aura that turns fire into dragon fire, teleporting, and the ability Spartoi, which at gold rank calls up a hundred dragon-tooth bone-golem warriors in blue and gold armour. Racial gift: his human gift Special Attack Affinity evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon and later into Hero's Drive, with the racial gift Hero's Sacrifice.
168.name: Humphrey Geller

169.content: Jason Asano is the series' protagonist: an Australian from the coastal town of Casselton Beach who, at twenty-three, is pulled across the cosmos to Pallimustus by a failed summoning. Humour and references: he jokes constantly and quotes films and television. He tells the Builder it and Knowledge "should get together and play Mario Kart"; he compares a projected face to Emperor Palpatine. He says "G'day" and "mate". Self-deprecation: "I'm only twenty-three but I've been pretty efficient about squandering my opportunities". He does not celebrate his birthday, which falls on 1 April: "It's not a celebratory time. I never liked my birthday anyway". Essences: Dark, Blood, Sin and the Doom confluence. His attributes are bound as Power (Blood), Speed (Dark), Spirit (Doom) and Recovery (the fourth essence). Weapons: a sword, Dread Salvation, an iron-rank growth item of legendary rarity made by Gary, later reforged by Gary with his mentor Virid and with Jason's soul-bond guiding the work, becoming the sword [Hegemon's Will] with the scabbard Hegemon's Dominion; Virid's surname Martine is Book 6, Ch47 L270. Way of the Reaper martial arts. The set Regalia of the Dark Hegemon includes the Amulet of the Dark Guardian. Abilities seen in the text: Path of Shadows, Midnight Eyes, Castigate and Verdict, Punition, Feast of Absolution and Gordon's Harbinger of Doom.
169.name: Jason Asano

170.content: Jeni Kavaloa is the gold-rank leader of the mixed-force surge expedition in Book 7. She is irritated by the roster, suspects Vesper Rimaros of assembling it, and enlists Jason's astral magic to seal the astral aperture. Impatient: unhappy about being "saddled with the mixed group". Suspicious of politics: the roster is like "a mad alchemist throwing volatile ingredients in a pot". Practical: she plans for the worst and does not slow when she senses the clearing's oddity. Gold rank; she senses Jason's defences pop an opponent's aura like a soap bubble. Sets up a device to seal the astral aperture, roping in Jason as astral specialist. She knows Orin Pensinata chiefly through his famous uncle Amos. Vesper Rimaros: suspected of rigging the roster. Jason: recruited for his astral skill.
170.name: Jeni Kavaloa

171.content: Kaito Asano is Jason's older brother, a year his senior, married to Amy, with two daughters, Hana and Jace. Easy-going and socially skilled, he is the "well-received original" Jason grew up in the shadow of. In Book 4 he reconnects with Jason, in Book 5 he flies a helicopter with Network defectors against the vampires, and he dies in Berlin. Socially adroit: Jason says he never had "Kaito's skill for getting along". The favourite: their parents "got Kaito, so they were willing to put up with me". Casual: he greets the family meeting with "G'day... We're arrived for the mysterious family meeting". Dry on pop culture: his knowledge of classic pop culture "appeared to begin and end with Miami Vice". Warm with his children: he leads Hana by the hand and carries Jace. After Jason's return he joins the Network-defector combat team with Asya and Greg. He flies drones to sweep the ruins of a town and owns the helicopter Jason and Akari ride in. A year older than Jason; the "well-received original" at school, so Jason felt like "a disappointing rehash". He and Amy bought her parents' house next door to Jason's family. He and Amy's relationship caused the fallout that left Jason dropping out of university; Jason did not want details. Jason: brother; Jason says Kaito made his own choice to stand up for his world and that Amy knows it. Amy: wife, with daughters Hana and Jace. Erika: sister who keeps the family together.
171.name: Kaito Asano

172.content: Ketevan Arziani is an analytical Network officer in Sydney, Anna Tilden's assistant, who later becomes Yumi Asano's chief of staff. Brisk and sceptical, she tests leaps of logic. Analytical: Anna places a lot of trust in her analytical abilities. Formal title: Assistant to the Director of Operations, Sydney branch. Investigates a hospital event up the coast. Jason saves her life with one of Shade's bodies forming a parachute. She leads the Network defectors' intake and sits on calls with the Sydney branch. After the Network's Australian branch breaks up, Yumi hires her for her administrative skill. Anna Tilden: her director. Yumi Asano: her new principal.
172.name: Ketevan Arziani

173.content: Knowledge is the goddess of Knowledge. Jason meets her in Book 1 on arriving at her temple, and for twelve books she charms and manipulates him.
173.name: Knowledge

174.content: Landemere Vane is the Vane heir whose failed summoning pulls Jason to Pallimustus. He is the first person Jason meets and the first he kills, which leaves Jason shaken for weeks. Ambitious and out of his depth: Dougall says Landemere summoned "one of them entities from beyond the void". Traditional family: his mother says "this is my manor, my family, and we do things the traditional way". Clive explains that Landemere's summoning went wrong, possibly because he reached beyond his ability or a dimensional event interfered. He was holding more than a thousand coins when killed. His mother, who looks no older than her son, is among the cultists who greet Jason. The Vane family treats the summoning as a family matter: "This is my manor, my family". Familiar: Jason's first encounter with a native creature was Vane's familiar, which tried to avenge him and fell victim to aging masonry. Cressida Vane: his mother, who calls him "poor Landemere".
174.name: Landemere Vane

175.content: Liara Rimaros is a gold-rank Adventure Society special-operations officer and a lesser member of the Rimaros royal house. She screens adventurers for Builder cultists in Book 7, leads the Book 8 expedition into the Builder's complex, handles Jason for the royal family and stays a brisk, protective ally. Brisk and official: she is working without rest as the city fills with adventurers to be filtered for cultists. Wary of politics: she "disdained" the politics she "could never seem to escape". Self-critical but resolute: after Gibson Amouz's capture she "allowed shame to flash over her expression before schooling it"; she stands up to his father, "Get out of my office, Lord Amouz". Protective: "Don't even think about it", she tells Zareen of Jason. Rank: a gold-ranker, leader of the Book 8 expedition with her former teammate Jana Costi as second. Investigator: her search for the cult's portal users is a process of elimination through portal schedules, market tracking and field reports. Not for rescues: she understands why she was told not to take part personally in the mining-complex rescue: "Her abilities were ill-suited to the task and her emotional investment would not be an asset". Royal branch: "from one of the more remote branches of the royal family", not close enough to be called a princess, but entitled to a home on the royal sky island and to take part in the contests for the throne in her youth.
175.name: Liara Rimaros

176.content: Lucian Lamprey is the corrupt director of Greenstone's Magic Society branch, an elf with a fighter's physique "banished to Greenstone for previous improprieties". He treats the Fortress as his office, orchestrates Jason's kidnapping with Cole Silva, and is cut down by Danielle Geller and imprisoned. Smug and indulgent: he arrives at his viewing room "with a contented sigh". Handsy: he strokes his fingers over a face in the viewing window. Quick to blame: his fury threatens to erupt when pressed. Danielle outpaces him in a duel and cuts him. His handling of a star seed for the Church of Purity comes under scrutiny. "Banished to Greenstone for previous improprieties"; he is not a member of the local elf community. His deputy Pochard maintains the city campus so he can use the Fortress as his office. Pochard Finn: deputy and friend. Cole Silva: co-conspirator. Danielle Geller: opponent.
176.name: Lucian Lamprey

177.content: Neil Davone is an elf of Greenstone's Island families, a healer who grows from the Mercers' hanger-on into the heart of Jason's team. He is a priest of the Healer, and by 2038 he uses his growth magic to reclaim deserts. Essences: Shield, Growth and Renewal, producing the Prosperity confluence: short-lived shields that intercept attacks, healing and cleansing. Abilities: size-growth power and Armour of Renewal, which reduces damage taken and gives healing over time; the Reaper's Redoubt. Summon: a chrysalis golem "like an ogre carved out of diamond" with runes appearing on its facets as it is hit. Late: his Growth, Renewal and Prosperity essences find fertile ground in desert reclamation in Australia and North Africa.
177.name: Neil Davone

178.content: Nicolas Hendren is the archbishop of the Church of Purity, a silver-rank barrier-and-force specialist who flees the inquiry and joins the Builder cult's camp before Jason's team kills him. Stiff, proud and rule-bound, he wants Purity's dignity even as it is dragged into the cult's plans. Disgruntled and proud: he is summoned to the cult camp and refuses to taint the church for "short-term power". Moral authority absent god: his god's voice is silent, making him the highest moral authority in the realm he stands in. Silver-rank barrier and force specialist: his barrier shields his group from a falling building; a force wave power; "always the true danger". Archbishop of the Church of Purity, introduced at a Greenstone meeting. One Book 3 line spells the name Hedron. The Builder cult: reluctant ally.
178.name: Nicolas Hendren

179.content: Padma Parsell is an adventurer from Remore Academy and Farrah's half-disciple, who leads a Vitesse team in the City of Fallen Echoes. Keen, grieving and quick to speak her mind, she treats Jason as a rival after Farrah's death. Keen and grieving: Farrah was her idol and mentor; she lets Jason vent her frustration. Obedient to instructors: Instructor Gabriel's voice triggers conditioned obedience. Ignores interruptions: when Lance calls out under his breath, she ignores him. Leader of a Vitesse team of Rufus's juniors. Trained at Remore Academy a few years behind Rufus. She had waited for Farrah's return to Vitesse and, when Farrah died, joined Emir's call for adventurers.
179.name: Padma Parsell

180.content: Pelli is a sharp-tongued core-using gold-ranker who keeps the town of Palisaros quiet and safe, is "Aunt Pelli" to the royal family, and is a contact for Jason in the Storm Kingdom. She fights a pirate captain outside Kasilaro and organises civilians at the mining facility. Blunt: "The name's Pelli and I'll thank you to use it". Teasing and self-deprecating: "I'm just an old core user"; she shakes her head at "an abundance of experience, dear gods". Protective: she fights outside the town to spare Kasilaro's residents. A gold-ranker and core user; she fights a pirate captain outside a town. She had a magic barrier put on a cave behind the waterfall. "Aunt Pelli" to Vesper from when she was a girl. Mayor-level authority in Palisaros: Argy tells Jason "You'll want to talk to Pelli". Vesper: calls her "Aunt Pelli". Rufus: she asks about his father and the sword.
180.name: Pelli

181.content: Rufus Remore is a bald, dark-skinned swordsman from Vitesse, grandson of the diamond-ranker Roland Remore. He is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, runs Jason's field assessment, and remains his friend for the rest of the series. He is calm under pressure: when Anisa demands that Jason be burned as tainted, he answers "I did [know]" and refuses her any say. He feels responsible as the leader of his group: Farrah tells Jason "Rufus is in charge, so he blames himself" for their capture, and says the pressure on him from his family is enormous. After Farrah's death he is driven by obsession, which strains his relationships. Swordsmanship: an elegant scimitar of golden light with red-gold inscriptions that he conjures in his hand; silver and golden swords. Other powers: boots that let him walk on water and a "speed of light" power that makes the world "seem to freeze in time" for "two seconds of accelerated time".
