Kingdom of Eclipse: a sun-and-moon power invoked by incantation. Teaching: he teaches Jason footwork, balance and combat and later teaches the Asano clan.
181.name: Rufus Remore

182.content: Sendira is Melody Jain's second in command in the Order of Redeeming Light's local enclave: a silver-rank zealot and the person Melody trusts most. She commands the Purity forces on the island in Book 8, carries the aura beacon and the clockwork kings, and holds the order's discipline together while suspecting others. Rank in the order: Melody leads the enclave and Sendira, her second, reports on what the scouts have found. The overall leadership is the same silver rank as the individual cell leaders, so there is "a constant tension". Reliability: she is "ever-reliable"; like another cell leader, Kelleigh, she is not ambitious, which places her as Melody's second. Doctrine: she tells the converted, "Only Purity is worthy of our devotion, not his servants... We are all unworthy, seeking to cleanse the taint that lingers within us", and "Distraction and frivolity taint pure dedication of purpose". Command on the island: she is "the commander of the Purity forces on the island", separating from most of her group to take a smaller team underground. Control of subordinates: she wants Fila and Ramona "under her thumb instead of causing trouble for Melody's plans". She snaps at Ramona that "What Melody wants with the target is no concern of yours. Your place is to obey, not criticise in ignorance".
182.name: Sendira

183.content: Sophie Wexler is a celestine fighter known as the Nightingale in the Greenstone fighting pits. She is a thief and debt-slave when Jason meets her, has her indenture taken over by Jason in Book 2, and becomes the team's fastest fighter and, later, Humphrey's fiancée. Essences: Swift, Balance and Wind, producing the Mystic confluence: Clive answers "Mystic" when Rufus asks what that combination produces. Before Jason's help she had only the Swift essence and its single ability for more than half a dozen years. Abilities: Eternal Moment, a massive acceleration power in which "time seemed to freeze" as she produced wind blades; Between the Raindrops; Mirage Step and Wind Blade; unarmed Way of the Reaper strikes. Racial gifts (celestine): Mana Integrity evolves into Mana Wellspring, Astral Affinity into Boundary Breaker, which removes the damage reduction from rank disparity, and Celestial Swiftness into Princess of the Firmament.
183.name: Sophie Wexler

184.content: Timos is a Builder cultist embedded in Greenstone for years who regrets going along with Thadwick's self-recruitment, kills Frank, and stands with Zato in the Vane estate ritual. He is careful, patient and horrified by amateurs. Regretful: he "quickly came to regret" Thadwick's aggressive self-recruitment. Cautious: every mistake "threatened to snowball into disaster". Compartmentalising: he facilitated the cult's insertions and ran operatives in compartmentalised groups. He kills Frank with a conjured spear. He takes part in a ritual with Zato and Dougall. "Timos had been operating in Greenstone for years". Thadwick: an inconvenient recruit.
184.name: Timos

185.content: Trenchant Moore is a gold-rank human sword specialist of the Sapphire Crown royal guard who escorts Jason's group in Rimaros. Watchful and reserved, he reads places and people for danger. Reserved: he drops to one knee before the royals. Cautious about politics: he warns that Vesper's world is political. Gold rank sword specialist who has served as a guard on and off for decades. He boards ships checking society contracts. The royal family does not shield the Sapphire Crown from surge quotas. Vesper Rimaros: the royal who gives him leave to keep his sword.
185.name: Trenchant Moore

186.content: A swordmaster prince of the Kingdom of Mirrors whom Clive meets in the City of Fallen Echoes; he is cheerful, reckless and a rival and friend to Jason's team. Introduces himself as "Valdis" and praises Clive's reputation; the system names him Valdis Volaire. A prince of the small but influential Kingdom of Mirrors, whose borders have not changed in eight centuries; his father, the Mirror King, is eight hundred years old and the kingdom is "thick with princes and princesses". A reckless enthusiast who leads his three teammates up a tower in search of treasure; he has a light-step power, a slow-fall power and a wall run. He chooses the path of courage in the trial and is the first to step forward. A sword master, mobile striker and the stronger team's leader; his team is a highly efficient cohort trained since before they had essences. His father collects him from Jason's ship, to Valdis's embarrassment; he portals in for Jason's memorial.
186.name: Valdis Volaire

187.content: Zara is a celestine princess of the Storm Kingdom, the "Hurricane Princess". Jason meets her in a tent during the contest for the Scythe of the Reaper, when she is nineteen and he is iron-rank. Years later the scandal of her false engagement claim, her loss of the succession, and her adoption into her mother's house bring her to Team Biscuit and, in 2038, into a romance with Jason. Powers: wind and water, big storms; recovery, speed, astral and holy affinity.
187.name: Zara Rimaros (Zara Nareen)

188.content: Zato is the silver-rank leader of the Builder cult's local forces in Book 3, a metal-bodied shapeshifter who recruits Thadwick, drives the cult's survivors to the Vane Estate and is the final opponent of Jason's team. He is competent, unfazed and sure of victory. On top of things: Jason says "He does seem pretty on top of things... I actually kind of like him" and invites him to join team "Hopelessly Outmatched". Convinced of victory: "Zato knew that his victory was imminent. He knew that the adventurers were no match for his power". Quiet in command: he stands with his back to the door, eyes lingering on Timos's neck marks, saying nothing. Recruiter: "I see your true potential". Silver rank, with a metal body of shifting abilities. Immovable in the final fight: no damage seems to impair him, even Humphrey's strikes. Trump card: after baiting out Sophie's absorb power, his body explodes into a mass of shrapnel. "The last silver-ranker left in the Builder cult's local forces"; tasked with leading the evacuation when the island stronghold was invaded, he escaped with a good number of people, though none of the other silver-rankers survived. Thadwick Mercer: his recruit. Humphrey and Sophie: opponents in the climax. Timos: his follower, whose neck he notices.
188.name: Zato

189.content: Jason's first familiar: a swarm of apocalypse leeches that lives in his blood, sprays out over enemies to bite and drain them, and can take the shape of a red-eyed blood clone of Jason. Colin begins as a hungry, wriggling swarm and grows into a being who talks back, waves from his bowl of leeches and calls Jason "smarmy". Named: Jason says, "I've decided to call him Colin. And his friends. Team Colin", and calls the swarm "Leechy" in the same fight. Lives in Jason's blood: Jason pricks his finger and the leeches crawl into his hand and vanish into his blood. His rapid regeneration only works while the familiar is in his bloodstream. Method: Jason sprays him out over a target like a fire hose and Colin crawls over armour to find flesh. Colin wiggles happily when pleased. Where he comes from: a summoned familiar is created through different means from the sanguine horror, but Clive observes it is what Jason summoned, and if Jason reached diamond his familiar would reach the full strength of a sanguine horror.
189.name: Colin

190.content: Jason's third familiar: an Avatar of Doom, a floating cloak holding a nebula in the shape of an eye, circled by blue and orange eye-orbs that fire beams. He cannot speak, but he answers questions with his orbs and has a distinct personality, and he is the key to the intrinsic-mandate magic Jason uses to work with authority. Summoned: the doom essence ability Avatar of Doom summons a familiar. At first it is unnamed, an iron-rank incorporeal familiar whose orbs make sustained beams, one of disruptive force and one of resonating force, and whose damage leaves Vulnerable. Named: asked if it wants a name, it flashes its blue orb, and Jason says, "I'm going to call you... Gordon". Orange is no and blue is yes: Gordon's orange orb flashes brightly as his signal for no. Shade relays him: "Gordon says that I should be last". Appearance: a disembodied cloak with a nebula-like cloud of blue and orange in the shape of an eye, and eyeball-patterned orbs drifting around it that fire unrelenting beams. In a fight: his beams inflict Vulnerable on a lizard; his energy dash is fast but his reflexes are sluggish, and a blow can dissipate his vessel entirely.
190.name: Gordon

191.content: Clive Standish's familiar: a rune tortoise whose shell carries runes that throw elemental attacks, and whose shell the whole team rides in, shelters in and runs the battlefield from. Onslow is gentle and a little stubborn, and Clive talks to him as "little buddy". First sight: Onslow is at the front of Clive's airboat with his head jutting forward "like a dog with its head out a car window". Clive sits on his shell with Jason beside him. Powers: he fires elemental attacks from the magic runes on his shell, which Clive recharges with his own mana. A rune dims when he takes a hit. A seat for the team: Clive picks up Stash and climbs on Onslow's shell with Neil, and the tortoise floats off the rooftop on a cushion of air. Clive drops down off him when the tower is threatened.
191.name: Onslow

192.content: Jason's shadow familiar, a formal, dry astral being who is one of the Reaper's shadows. He first appears as the keeper of the Reaper trials, becomes Jason's closest and most constant companion, and acts as his butler, driver, spy and sounding board. He says himself that he is a shepherd of death, and that he has changed more than the others of his kind. The invigilator: he appears as the shadowy figure who runs the trials of the City of Fallen Echoes and offers to explain their practical dangers or their origins. He hands out vials and medallions with his shadowy hands, which are cold to the touch. A familiar before: he tells the competitors that the grandmaster who built the place was an outworlder with the dark essence like Jason, "I was his summoned familiar once". Summoned by Jason: when Jason chooses to summon a familiar after the trials, he greets Shade with "I was hoping it would be you". Bodies: he appears as three bodies that become horses for a ride or large lizards for rough terrain, and his bodies move among monsters as elusive shadowy figures. The Reaper's child: the Reaper says "Of all my children, Shade has ever followed his own path".
192.name: Shade

193.content: Belinda Callahan's astral lantern: a small living lantern that orbits her, projects shields, fires force bolts and feeds mana to her team. It is the quietest of the team's familiars, but it is on the field in almost every battle. Summoned: the final ability of Belinda's power set is a summoned familiar, an astral lantern. Belinda names it: "How about Shimmer?". In a fight: it projects shields to protect the team and, with Gordon, beams the enemy to split their attention. The force bolts of a lantern familiar prove more dangerous to its own side against Hendren's defences.
193.name: Shimmer

194.content: Humphrey Geller's bonded familiar: a baby mirage dragon whose full name is Velitraxistaasch, who prefers "Stash". He changes shape constantly, starts as a barking lizard, a bird or a puppy and ends up large enough to crush a company of messengers, and he talks, mostly in cheerful, blunt remarks. Name: "It's short for Velitraxistaasch. He likes 'Stash,' though.". Jason works out what he is at once and Humphrey is startled. Bond: "Our mothers arranged him becoming my familiar. Or me becoming his person, depending on how you look at it". A bonded familiar is an actual magical creature that can die, unlike a summoned familiar. Shapes: a canary on Humphrey's head and a puppy, a bird that swoops from the sky and turns into a puppy in his arms, a barking lizard, and a bark lurker or a darting bird in a fight. Biscuits: Jason feeds him a biscuit and he turns into a puppy to snuffle it from Jason's hand, then yaps his agreement. Speech: "Stash chase worm! Stash chase worm!". Scouting: he leads Humphrey's party by barking in the right direction to the margolls. Special attack: Humphrey's racial ability evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon.
194.name: Stash

key: The One Day War (War of Four Cities)
195.comment: The One Day War (War of Four Cities)
195.content: During the Rimaros monster surge, the Builder cult sends mobile cities against the Storm Kingdom: a ground city that walks south, an underwater city and a flying fortress-city that appears over Livaros. The adventurers answer with six diamond-rankers, gods' miracles and a single true bomb carried into the flying city. The war is later called the War of Four Cities or the One Day War.
keys: The One Day War (War of Four Cities)
195.name: The One Day War (War of Four Cities)

key: Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)
Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh
196.comment: Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)
196.content: After a four-month journey south from Rimaros, Jason's convoy reaches the rainforest elf city of Yaresh as messengers besiege it. The Church of Knowledge gathers an army in the background, the messengers use apocalypse beasts and world-taker worms as weapons, and the battle ends with a breach the messengers' commander Marek has to concede. Jason's identity as an astral king comes out, and Marek and Tera become his captives. Messenger agents in the city: Benella presents Jason to Kaal as a threat; Fal Vin Garath calls Shade "Reaper spawn". Apocalypse beasts and worms: Carlos suspects a heat-consuming parasite with a swarm hive mind; "[Inexorable Doom] on [World-Taker Worm]"; the messengers know the apocalypse beasts and use them as weapons. Defence plans: the two cloud palaces are reconfigured into defence bunkers; Hana directs the clergy away from Jason's bunker. The trigger: an Adventure Society functionary hides his anger behind an aura mask; a naga egg is triggered in the city. The breach: Marek Nior Vargas leads the breach force over the entertainment district; the breach is a trap. Eilaf Hayel commands the defence of the entertainment district. Intervention: Raythe tells Schaat "Leave Asano be. Turn around and leave this city"; Schaat is found dead. The duel: Tera Jun Casta challenges Jason; Jason's last word stops her dead.
keys: Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)
Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh
196.name: Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)

key: Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)
Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone
197.comment: Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)
197.content: For about a year after the Reaper trials, a hidden cult of the Builder works inside Greenstone's aristocracy and through the church of Purity. It implants star seeds, suborns Thadwick Mercer and others, and prepares to claim an astral space. Jason's team learns of it in Book 2 and breaks it in Book 3, ending in the astral space the cult built and the death of Jason.
keys: Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)
Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone
197.name: Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)

key: Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves (Books 4-6)
Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves
198.comment: Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves (Books 4-6)
198.content: Jason wakes on Earth in early June, a year and a half after he left. Earth's magic is rising; the Network, the Cabal and the Engineers of Ascension fight for influence, monsters arrive in waves, vampires rise, and Jason builds a family compound, a clan and his first Earth domains. The era ends with Jason leaving Earth, in a warm French autumn.
keys: Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves (Books 4-6)
Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves
198.name: Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves (Books 4-6)

199.content: After Farrah's death, Emir Bahadir opens an astral space in the delta and invites iron-rank teams to compete for the legacy of the Order of the Reaper. The City of Fallen Echoes holds the trials, a shipful of time-displaced priests and a Reaper-run test of virtue. Jason's team wins a set of rewards, and the tale of the Order's survival becomes a live question. Launch: iron-rankers board the cloud ship once the palace has resumed its shape; adventurers spread across Sky Scar Lake by every means. The zone is "City of Fallen Echoes (Gate Tower Three)". Shade's account: the legacy goes to whoever embodies the ideals of the Order; the last grandmaster sent all the initiates into the city; the vorger do not kill, and the initiates were turned into abominations. The city: siege golems and flesh abominations adapt to how they are fought. Imran Keane joins Jason's party. A blood root vine is hit with Inexorable Doom. Rival teams: Padma's team is the last to join, and Beth's team stays put beside Jason's near the end. Before the trials Beth's and Rick's teams had met in the mirage chamber contest. All reach the city centre, where Humphrey's team staggers in ragged. The final day: Shade announces that the second trial ends in one day and warns of nightmare hags, diamond-rank astral entities. Rewards include a True Light, Summoner's Die: Form and an Immortal Crest.
199.name: Era Guide: The Reaper Trials (Book 2)

200.content: Jason returns to Pallimustus at the standing stones in a cyclone, just as a long-delayed monster surge begins. In the Storm Kingdom he meets its royal family, settles at Palisaros, helps defeat the Builder's invasion in the One Day War, and then faces the Order of Redeeming Light, a mining complex rescue and the birth of his astral kingdom. The era ends with the Builder withdrawing and Jason technically an astral king.
200.name: Era Guide: The Rimaros Surge (Books 7-8)

201.content: Single-use stones that awaken an essence ability, found, traded and rewarded by rank and rarity. What they do: "An awakening stone that unlocks the power of consumption... Effect: Awakens an essence ability", requiring an unawakened essence ability. The stone melts into the user's hand "with little fanfare". Why they matter: Rufus tells Jason he cannot "properly progress towards bronze rank until you awaken every essence ability you have. That's all twenty". Naming and rarity: stones are "unranked" and carry a rarity, such as the Awakening Stone of the Feast, of Adventure, of the Stars and of the Reaper. Affinity: the Reaper stone "sharing affinity with the Reaper" is used in Jason's awakening ritual with the Reaper token, and it gives Humphrey, a human, a special attack. Divine awakening stones: a god-made stone is "transcendent rank, epic" and bestows a specific aura power. Sources: looting an awakening stone or essence can pay better than the contract to kill the monster; the Adventure Society gives stones for exceptional service, "although rarely", and some open contracts offer them as rewards; otherwise stones are bought through brokers, almost always at auction, at exorbitant prices. Brokers in a small city hold the valuable stuff, like essences and stones, for big auctions. Family supply: the Gellers traditionally supply their scions with enough stones to get started, while the rest must be earned.
201.name: Awakening Stones

202.content: The badge as an object: how an Adventure Society badge is made, tied to its wearer, tracked, altered and replaced, and what a guild membership adds on top. The organisation file explains what the Society does with badges; this file is about the item and the ways it fails. Who makes it: the Adventure Society manages the badges but the Magic Society creates them, taking an aura imprint from the new member inside a magic circle in about a minute. What it carries: every badge is paired with a tracking stone that tells the Society whether the member is alive or dead and finds them if they go missing. Members claim adventure notices with it and hold it against a security screen to close a contract. The wallet: the badge is a circular iron medallion embossed with a sword and rod crossed over a shield, carried in a leather wallet. Stars are on the metal: an official taps a wedge-shaped stone to the badge and a star is added, or removed. It tracks the badge, not the person: the tracking stones trace the badges, so a discarded badge hides its owner. A change of aura leaves the imprint on the badge unmatched, so the wearer cannot be tracked until a new badge is issued. When the Society wanted people's auras re-examined, their badges were also to be replaced. Jason's case: the stone cannot track his aura imprint, and Farrah says some people have abilities that block magical tracking.
202.name: Badges and Guild Membership

203.content: Emir's cloud ship and palace, and Jason's own cloud houses, yachts and palaces made from his Cloud Flask. Emir's cloud ship: it arrives at the Greenstone dock and a walkway of cloud connects to the shore as a hole opens in its side. Moored, it morphs over about ten minutes into a palace of clouds floating on the water. Emir's cloud palace: floating just offshore on the north side of the Island, "fully exposed to the waves and currents, yet remained as immovable as solid ground", with wings and towers in blue, purple, orange and gold. Walls, floors and ceilings glow with absorbed sunlight the palace stores and distributes, and the floors have a bouncy-castle spring. Low-magic limits: out of Greenstone the ship's full functionality is restored when Emir's cloud ship floats above Kurdansk. Team base: Jason's team move into Emir's palace after the contest. Jason's Cloud Flask: it creates buildings and vehicles of cloud, with forms limited by rank, iron cloud houses, bronze cloud vehicles and silver cloud palaces; items inside a returned construct are stored in a dimensional space until another is formed. Asano Village: Farrah prepares a place for Jason's cloud house at the end of a glass tunnel along the seafloor, two kilometres out, reached by a tramway from the compound and sealed by a wall of water, so the house can run underwater; the text checked does not show the house later sitting there.
203.name: Cloud Constructs and Cloud Palaces

key: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
204.comment: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
204.content: Single-use and crafting items: the City of Fallen Echoes rewards, clockwork cores, reality cores and star seeds. Lesser Miracle Potion: "iron rank, legendary", "Salvation in a bottle", it fully restores health, mana and stamina but only works on normal and iron-rank people, and its lingering magic delays other recovery. Medallion of Escape: "silver rank, uncommon", evacuates the holder from the astral space when their aura is projected into it, and only works inside the City of Fallen Echoes. Immortal Crest: "iron rank, rare", lets a mystical tattooist draw out a soul crest and only works on an iron-rank essence user. Summoner's Die: Form: "iron rank [growth], legendary", it randomly alters the form of an iron-rank summon. Clockwork Core: "iron rank, rare", the core of an artificial monster that simplifies the materials and processes of a construct creature; clockwork cores are made by clockwork kings. Star seeds: great astral beings, not gods, "can send their followers star seeds"; once implanted and germinated the body transforms, "minor or major". Reality cores: roughly the size and shape of an ostrich egg, dark crystal glowing with transcendent light; one appears in each affected zone and the factions scramble for it. They are the source of the transformation zones' treasures and are common in node space.
keys: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
204.name: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials

key: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
205.comment: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
205.content: The vehicles that cross the desert around Greenstone: the sand skimmers and sand barges Emir Bahadir's people run, the carriages that move expeditions to relay stations, and the monstrous Ustei war barge. Emir's cloud ship is covered in Cloud_Constructs_and_Palaces.md. Sand skimmers: small desert vehicles that carry a party across the sand. Emir leaves skimmers waiting at Boko to carry the team into the desert. Pushed past their limits: one of Emir's people specialises in magical tools and can periodically push the skimmers to speeds beyond their normal capability, so the whole vehicle vibrates. Their limits: skimmers cannot go through an astral-space aperture, so the party continues on foot. Requisitioned skimmers: expeditions requisition extra skimmers from the city and return them afterwards. Sand barges: larger vessels that move people and supplies overland. After Emir's ship sails south down the coast and into shore at an unremarkable patch of desert, his people unload three sand barges that carry the whole group inland to Sky Scar Lake. The trip takes hours more, into the night. Expedition transport: an expedition leaving Greenstone uses carriages to reach desert relay stations, then the captured Ustei barge and smaller barges supplied by the Magic Society.
keys: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
205.name: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges

206.content: How things and people are carried across a world without carts or roads: storage spaces that hold a person's goods, dimensional bags that expand them, and portal abilities that move people between places they have seen. Jason's own inventory and shadow gates are the best-documented examples, and the rest of the world treats both as everyday professional tools with hard limits. Jason's inventory is "a video-game inventory only Jason could see", unlike Clive's storage, which is opened by making a circle of floating runes with a portal inside. Dimensional bags are items with a rank. They add slots to an inventory in proportion to their rank, and at iron rank one bag slot is available and holds only iron-rank bags. Bags come in novelty shapes, such as a pair of boots. Storage as a profession: adventurers carry their possessions in dimensional bags or dimensional space abilities and travel light. Some portal workers "aren't even adventurers and do storage space transport for a living". Loot goes straight in: looted coins appear in the storage abilities of Clive, Humphrey and Jason, and Jason keeps a ledger of how much belongs to whom. Storage can be looted: Jason could have taken the items from Farrah's storage space by looting her body like a monster, and neither man suggested such a defilement. Limits on contents: it is "almost impossible to place living material inside dimensional storage", with only a few carefully chosen plants viable.
206.name: Dimensional Storage and Portals

207.content: The reforged form of Jason's sword Dread Salvation and the scabbard that was made with it. Hegemon's Will is the weapon and Hegemon's Dominion is the scabbard; the game treats them as one item. The scabbard stores afflictions that land on Jason and turns them against the next enemy he cuts. Soul_Bound_Items_and_Regalia.md covers where the sword came from; this file covers what the two pieces do. Hegemon's Dominion: "silver rank [growth], legendary", "the scabbard to Hegemon's Will" and "the embodiment of hegemonic control, representing the hegemon's mastery of his domain". Bound to Jason: it cannot be used by anyone else, shares his ability to ignore rank disparity, and is "treated as the same item" as the sword for all magical effects. What the scabbard does: afflictions affecting the wielder are periodically moved to it, which removes their effects from him but is not a cleansing effect. The rate depends on the effects' rank relative to the wielder; suppressing the originator's aura speeds the transfer and being aura suppressed slows it. If the sword is sheathed, all afflictions pass to the weapon and affect the next enemy struck. Anything the target resists or is immune to is negated and cannot be passed to another target. Growth: its growth is no longer capped by rank, but the upgrade materials are ones Jason has never heard of and are presumably gold rank.
207.name: Hegemon's Will and Hegemon's Dominion

208.content: Jason's combat robes are the flowing, tailored armour that gives him his dark, shadowy look. The first is the Trap Weaver Battle Robe, bought from Gilbert Bertinelli in Book 1; it is replaced at each rank by a new robe made by Gilbert from monster materials Jason supplies. The robes are armour in a robe's cut, stored in his inventory and swapped on by the outfits tab.
208.name: Jason's Combat Robes

209.content: Reality cores are egg-sized crystals of concentrated power found at transformation events on Earth. Factions fight over them, vampires use them to power their blood, and Jason's work shuts the supply off. Genesis cores are different: Jason loots them from anomalies in the zones to expand his spirit domain.
209.name: Reality Cores and Genesis Cores

key: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
210.comment: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
210.content: Jason's three soul-bound growth items, joined in Book 6 into the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon by the Soul-Imprinting Triune, plus the Robes of the Astral Verdict. Dread Salvation: a sword "crafted with gratitude, in hope it would be of the greatest use in the moment of greatest need"; "iron rank [growth], legendary"; when an affliction special attack meets a physical immunity it gains Stone Cutter, and for a magical immunity Spell Breaker. Gary made it, as a gift. Dread Salvation in Book 6: bronze rank, bound to Jason and sharing his ability to ignore rank disparity; it can be imbued with aura for damage at an ongoing mana cost; "The original creator must demonstrate his growth and reforge the weapon". The window says it "must be reforged by the original craftsperson in order to advance further". The reforged sword is named Hegemon's Will on its item screen, with its scabbard Hegemon's Dominion treated as the same item; Gary gives it to Jason in Book 7. The reforging by Gary and Virid is Book 7, Ch2 L73-74. Cloud Flask: iron rank growth item that Jason binds in Book 2; it creates cloud buildings and vehicles, with forms limited by rank. By Book 6 it is silver rank, with the cloud house at iron, cloud vehicle at bronze and cloud palace at silver. Its maker is "some unknown diamond-rank craftsman".
keys: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
210.name: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon

key: The Builder's Door and the Fundament Gate
211.comment: The Builder's Door and the Fundament Gate
211.content: The Builder's astral door, the Fundament Gate that Jason absorbs, and how they let him work in the fundamental realm. The door: Mr North tells Jason "It's not a literal door... It's an astral construct with the power to manifest in physical reality in the form of a portal", and that Jason must absorb it so it cannot be taken from him. Jason notes "This door is an object of the Builder". The Fundament Gate: a ring of rough marble standing stones in a dell, "transcendent rank, legendary", whose window lets Jason incorporate it into his Spirit Vault, purging the Builder's influence. It improves his sense of Builder items and adds to Path of Shadows the ability to open a portal to the Fundamental Realm. Consequences: Jason used the Builder's door when he flooded himself with magic and later "accidentally trashed it for parts"; "the magic of the Builder's door that Jason had absorbed" is distinct from the soul-attack trick he learned from the star seed. Builder's view: in Book 6 Shako says that without the Fundament Gate the Builder forged, Jason could not have remade the zone, and Dawn asks for the designs so the World-Phoenix can create a complementary item to anchor the bridge. Later items: the Fundamental Realm Authority Token and the Firmamental Bridge Anchor are looted from the destroyed artefacts; see Tokens_Stones_and_Relics.md.
keys: The Builder's Door and the Fundament Gate
211.name: The Builder's Door and the Fundament Gate

212.content: Transcendent-rank items that mark the favour or authority of great astral beings and gods: astral blessing tokens, divine awakening stones, the Fundamental Realm Authority Token and the Cup of Heroes. Astral blessing tokens: Clive says they are "something great astral beings give out to bestow blessings, as signs of approval"; they trigger racial gift evolutions, and are harmless, unlike star seeds. World-Phoenix Token: Jason finds it in his starting inventory, "transcendent rank, legendary", "Uses remaining: 1/1" with unreadable effects. It is consumed in Book 3. Reaper Token: an obsidian square engraved with a silver scythe, "transcendent rank, legendary". Jason takes the Scythe of the Reaper by placing his inventory window behind it, and the token is added. It is melded into his body with the awakening stone of the Reaper in Clive's ritual and consumed. Knowledge's token: a small stone square like the World-Phoenix Token but washed-out blue, offered with two awakening stones; Jason is told it would take him home and wonders whether to trust it.
212.name: Tokens, Stones and Relics
